title: Gemini Fills COO Post It Left Empty in February With Ex-Treasury Official
summary:

content:
2026-11-24T08:46:57.005+02:00

Tuesday, 24/11/2026 | 06:46 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • John York led workforce cuts of about 28,000 people in government before joining the crypto exchange in July.
  • The company has cut operating expenses for three quarters in a row and shed about a quarter of its staff.

Gemini Space Station named John York chief operating officer, a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed yesterday (Monday). He had run operations at the crypto exchange operator as a vice president.

The appointment fills a post Gemini left open in February, when it said it did not intend to name a successor to the departing chief operating officer.

York, 45, came to Gemini from the US Department of the Treasury, where he was most recently assistant secretary for management. According to the filing, he led workforce reductions there that lowered headcount by about 28,000 people and saved about $5 billion a year.

Gemini has been cutting too. In February the company said it would reduce its size by roughly 25% and close its accounts in the UK, the EU and Australia.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Expenses Fall for a Third Quarter

Operating expenses fell 30% year-over-year to $119.9 million in the third quarter, the company reported on November 12. It cited lower headcount after the February reduction in force.

Chief Executive Tyler Winklevoss said in the results release that Gemini intends "to stay disciplined about where those dollars go."

The net loss narrowed to $58.6 million from $159.5 million a year earlier. In the second quarter Gemini lost $107.7 million, while its new prediction markets business brought in about $500,000 of revenue.

The February cut went deeper than recent rounds at Coinbase or at Gemini itself. Coinbase announced a 14% reduction in May that affected about 693 employees, FM Intelligence data show.

Gemini cut 10%, 7% and 10% of its staff in three rounds between June 2022 and January 2023. By the company's own count, its workforce peaked at about 1,100 in 2022 and had halved by the end of 2025, before the latest cut.

A Post Left Open Since February

Marshall Beard left as chief operating officer on February 17, along with Chief Financial Officer Dan Chen and Chief Legal Officer Tyler Meade.

Co-founder Cameron Winklevoss, the president of Gemini, took on many of Beard's duties, including revenue-generating responsibilities, the company said at the time.

York's appointment took effect on November 18. His pay did not change, according to the filing, which puts his base salary at $400,000 a year with a target bonus of 20% of that amount.

He joined Gemini in July. Before Treasury, York was a senior manager at Accenture Federal Services and worked at the US Office of Personnel Management from 2019 to 2021. He began his career as an officer in the US Coast Guard.

title: Summit Day: London’s Trading and Fintech Community Meets at Old Billingsgate
summary: The Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 is taking place today, 24 November, at Old Billingsgate, with a full conference programme that spans between artificial intelligence, retail brokerage, digital assets, liquidity, regulation and emerging trading products, with speakers from across the industry....

  • The Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 experience starts now.

The Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 is taking place today, 24 November, at Old Billingsgate, with a full conference programme that spans between artificial intelligence, retail brokerage, digital assets, liquidity, regulation and emerging trading products, with speakers from across the industry.

Alongside the sessions, attendees can explore the exhibition, meet participating companies and connect with industry professionals face-to-face. Review the schedule to prioritise the discussions that matter most to your business.

The summit will bring together industry professionals from brokerage, institutional trading, fintech, liquidity, payments and financial technology. The event's 15th edition combines conference discussions, an exhibition and opportunities to build relationships in one focused day.

Beyond the stages, the exhibition offers the opportunity to meet companies developing products and services for the industry. Attendees can use their time to compare approaches, discuss operational challenges and reconnect with contacts. Business Connect roundtables provide additional focused discussions for participants whose separate applications have been approved.

Following the Opening Networking Blitz at The Folly on 23 November, today's Summit is the central opportunity to turn plans into real conversations. Whether attending for intelligence, partnerships or practical solutions, delegates can make the most of the day by prioritising the people and topics that matter to them.

Delegates can move between sessions on AI, brokerage growth, liquidity, stablecoins and market regulation while using the exhibition to meet the companies building and supporting financial-services products.

For those who joined the Opening Networking Blitz at The Folly on 23 November, the main event offers an opportunity to build on those discussions . Whether the objective is to assess a provider, hear a new perspective or develop a partnership, Old Billingsgate brings the people and discussions together in one focused day.

View today’s agenda here and register onsite.

title: High-Yield Crypto Promos Trapped Chinese Investors in Bitmart Collapse: Nikkei
summary: ,Cryptocurrency exchange Bitmart is in a severe financial crisis after revealing a $319.5 million shortfall alongside just $1.9 million in liquid assets available to repay users. A report explains how high-yield promotions lured in new users amid the collapse. Internal Control Failures and Declining...
content:
,Cryptocurrency exchange Bitmart is in a severe financial crisis after revealing a $319.5 million shortfall alongside just $1.9 million in liquid assets available to repay users. A report explains how high-yield promotions lured in new users amid the collapse.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitmart disclosed a $319.5 million shortfall with only $1.9 million in liquid assets for customer payouts.
  • Exploited rebates and a 14.2% drop in top-10 exchange spot trading volume accelerated Bitmart’s collapse.
  • At least 74 Bitmart creditors holding $34 million hired counsel to fight dollar-based claim conversions.

Internal Control Failures and Declining Revenue

Cryptocurrency exchange Bitmart is facing a deepening financial crisis after disclosing a $319.5 million shortfall and reporting just $1.9 million in liquid assets available for customer repayments. Furthermore, several users reported being unable to access their cryptocurrency holdings despite Bitmart’s previous assurances.

According to a Nikkei Asia report, Bitmart disclosed its limited liquidity to financial adviser Alvarez & Marsal, which is overseeing the restructuring process. The revelations have raised questions about the exchange’s financial management, customer asset protections, and the prospects of recovering funds trapped on the platform.

Several Bitmart customers, including investors in China, were drawn to the platform’s high-yield savings promotions rather than speculative cryptocurrency trading. Some deposited substantial funds into short-term savings products—such as 14-day offerings advertising annualized yields of up to 18.8%—which significantly exceeded the returns available through conventional savings options.

The exchange reportedly continued marketing short-term investment products in the weeks leading up to its closure announcement.

Some former Bitmart employees cited in the report said the exchange’s financial difficulties began emerging months before its closure announcement. One unnamed former employee said revenue from token listings declined from approximately $1 million in October 2025 to $250,000 in June 2026.

The deterioration coincided with broader weakness in centralized cryptocurrency trading, as evidenced by Coingecko’s third-quarter industry report, which showed that spot trading volumes across the 10 largest centralized exchanges fell 14.2% quarter over quarter to $1.65 trillion.

However, former employees suggested Bitmart’s problems extended beyond declining trading volumes, pointing to inadequate internal controls that allowed groups of traders to exploit the exchange’s rebate and zero-slippage incentive programs. The exchange has since admitted that certain groups exploited incentive policies, generating financial losses.

One former employee also claimed finance personnel identified the activity months before the shutdown, but failed to escalate the findings to senior management promptly.

Creditor Pushback Over Restructuring Terms

Meanwhile, Bitmart’s restructuring efforts are facing resistance from customers concerned about potentially substantial losses and the legal treatment of their cryptocurrency holdings. At least 74 customers representing approximately $34 million in assets have formed an informal creditor group and appointed Jack Ding, a cross-border dispute lawyer, as legal counsel.

A central dispute concerns Bitmart’s proposal to convert customers’ cryptocurrency balances into dollar-denominated claims. Ding argued that the exchange’s user agreement recognizes customers as owners of the cryptocurrency held in their accounts. He said converting those holdings into monetary claims could undermine those ownership rights.

The restructuring process has also attracted criticism over the continued involvement of Bitmart’s existing management.

Meanwhile, the exchange’s collapse has highlighted the risks facing Chinese cryptocurrency investors who increasingly rely on offshore trading platforms. China banned cryptocurrency trading, mining, and related business activities in 2021, although individuals can still legally possess digital assets.

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned that investors using unregulated cryptocurrency platforms could lose their entire holdings if an exchange collapses, suffers a cyberattack, or misappropriates customer assets.

Despite the restrictions, offshore exchanges continue attracting Chinese investors seeking higher returns amid low domestic interest rates and limited access to foreign investment products.

For Bitmart customers, the immediate concern remains whether the restructuring process will return a meaningful portion of their cryptocurrency holdings. With the exchange reporting only $1.9 million in liquid assets available to repay a much larger shortfall, the scale and timing of potential customer recoveries remain uncertain.

title: Bitcoin Reserves Just Found a New Use on Wall Street, but There’s a Catch
summary: Key takeaways CFTC staff guidance issued on November 23 says swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and clearinghouses may count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. The advisory references a minimum 20% haircut for Bitcoin...
content:
Key takeaways

  • CFTC staff guidance issued on November 23 says swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and clearinghouses may count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements.
  • The advisory references a minimum 20% haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, so a $10 million Bitcoin reserve would count as $8 million, and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins.
  • Crypto cannot be used to meet the separate cash and liquid-resources requirement, which covers three months for swap execution facilities and generally six months for the other two types of venue.
  • It is a staff advisory, not a binding rule, and nothing in it requires institutions to buy Bitcoin.

Bitcoin reserves have found another potential use within the US financial system. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has clarified that regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ethereum and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. However, the regulator is not prepared to treat those holdings like cash.

The guidance, issued on November 23, could give regulated trading venues greater flexibility in managing their balance sheets. For Bitcoin investors, however, the more interesting question is whether that flexibility will translate into fresh institutional demand.

The answer is not quite as straightforward as it might seem.

CFTC Gives Bitcoin Reserves a New Role in Financial Markets

The CFTC’s latest advisory addresses three types of regulated businesses: swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations.

These institutions are required to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover at least one year of operating costs. Under the new staff guidance, Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins may contribute toward those requirements, subject to appropriate valuation discounts.

The announcement follows broader efforts to integrate digital assets into regulated financial infrastructure. NewsBTC previously reported on the CFTC’s guidance concerning tokenized collateral at clearinghouses, another area where traditional financial markets are gradually accommodating blockchain-based assets.

This time, the discussion is not about what traders can post as collateral. It is about the assets that the institutions running those markets can rely on to keep their businesses operating.

For a company that already holds Bitcoin, the clarification could make those holdings more useful from a regulatory standpoint. For businesses considering adding cryptocurrency to their balance sheets, it removes some uncertainty surrounding how those assets would be recognized.

But that recognition comes at a discount!

A $10 Million Bitcoin Reserve Is Worth $8 Million on Paper

The CFTC advisory references a minimum 20% valuation haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, consistent with earlier staff treatment of proprietary cryptocurrency positions held by futures commission merchants.

Qualifying payment stablecoins receive considerably more favorable treatment, with a referenced haircut of 2%.

An exchange holding $10 million in Bitcoin, for example, would be able to count $8 million toward the relevant financial resource requirement if it applied a 20% haircut and no further deductions were necessary.

The remaining $2 million is not a realized loss. It is a regulatory adjustment intended to account for the risk associated with holding a volatile asset.

Crypto assets that are neither readily marketable nor qualifying payment stablecoins would generally face a 100% haircut, effectively excluding them from the calculation.

Perhaps the most revealing part of the advisory is the regulator’s warning about what it calls wrong-way risk.

The CFTC staff specifically states:

“

A DCM should consider potential wrong-way risk

For a cryptocurrency-focused exchange, that risk is particularly relevant. A prolonged Bitcoin sell-off could put pressure on trading revenues while simultaneously reducing the value of the assets the exchange relies on to support its operations.

The problem is not simply that Bitcoin is volatile. It is that its value could deteriorate at precisely the moment a crypto business finds itself under financial pressure.

A 20% valuation discount provides some protection against that scenario, but it is hardly a guarantee.

The CFTC Is Still Drawing a Line Between Bitcoin and Cash

Despite allowing digital assets to contribute toward broader operating resources, the CFTC has maintained a separate requirement for cash and highly liquid securities.

Bitcoin, Ethereum and even qualifying payment stablecoins cannot be used to satisfy that particular obligation under the advisory.

Swap execution facilities must maintain qualifying liquid resources sufficient to cover at least three months of projected operating expenses or the cost of winding down their operations, whichever is greater.

For designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations, the operating-cost liquidity requirement generally covers at least six months.

The distinction matters because an institution can have substantial assets on its balance sheet without necessarily having the cash available to meet immediate obligations.

It is also worth noting that the guidance does not address whether cryptocurrencies can satisfy the separate financial resources that clearinghouses must maintain to cover clearing-member defaults.

In effect, the CFTC is recognizing Bitcoin as an asset that can contribute to an institution’s financial strength without giving it the same regulatory standing as cash.

That is a more cautious approach than some Bitcoin advocates might have hoped for, but arguably a more sustainable one for integrating cryptocurrency into financial infrastructure.

Could the Decision Trigger More Institutional Bitcoin Buying?

The bullish interpretation is relatively simple. If regulated financial institutions can derive greater utility from holding Bitcoin, more of them may eventually consider allocating capital to the cryptocurrency.

There is some merit to that argument.

The expansion of regulated crypto infrastructure has already brought digital assets closer to traditional financial markets. Earlier, NewsBTC reported on Coinbase’s CFTC registration for its USDC-focused derivatives clearinghouse, illustrating how cryptocurrency businesses are increasingly operating within established regulatory frameworks.

The latest advisory gives relevant institutions another reason to evaluate how digital assets fit into their balance sheets.

Still, there is a considerable difference between allowing an institution to hold Bitcoin for regulatory purposes and giving it an economic incentive to buy more.

An exchange that already owns Bitcoin could benefit from the clarification without purchasing a single additional coin. Another might conclude that holding conventional securities remains more efficient, particularly given the valuation discounts and separate liquidity requirements.

Nothing in the advisory requires institutions to acquire Bitcoin, and no purchase commitments were disclosed alongside the announcement.

Investors should therefore resist the temptation to translate this development directly into a bullish price forecast.

The longer-term significance may be greater than the immediate market impact. Every additional recognized use for Bitcoin within regulated financial markets strengthens the case for its utility beyond speculative trading.

However, the November 23 document remains a staff advisory rather than a binding rule adopted by the full Commission. It does not amend existing regulations or create enforceable rights.

The next meaningful development will be evidence that regulated institutions are actually changing their reserve allocations in response.

Until then, Bitcoin has gained another form of regulatory recognition. Whether it gains another source of sustained buying pressure is a different question entirely.

title: The Hidden Cost of 24/7 Payments: Fragmented Liquidity Is Tying Up Broker Capital
summary:
A broker can have millions in available capital and still struggle to meet a customer withdrawal.
The problem isn't necessarily a lack of funds. It's where those funds are held, the currency they're denominated in and whether they can be accessed when needed.
As stablecoins make round-the-clock sett...
content:
A broker can have millions in available capital and still struggle to meet a customer withdrawal.

The problem isn't necessarily a lack of funds. It's where those funds are held, the currency they're denominated in and whether they can be accessed when needed.

As stablecoins make round-the-clock settlement possible, this disconnect is becoming increasingly important. Payment infrastructure has accelerated, but the treasury operations supporting it haven't always kept pace.

For brokers, the consequences extend beyond delayed payments. Fragmented liquidity creates unnecessary funding requirements, increases operational costs and ties up capital that could otherwise be deployed more productively.

24/7 settlement isn't simply a back-office processing challenge. It's increasingly a question of capital efficiency.

The challenge: quantifying fragmented liquidity

Consider how a typical international brokerage operates.

It has several PSP and banking relationships in different countries. It is managing multiple currencies and holding digital assets across several wallets. Maybe it’s also operating through separate legal entities, each with its own accounts and regulatory obligations.

A necessary structure, but one that can create a fragmented picture of the company's available funds.

One PSP account may be overfunded while another runs short. Meanwhile, idle fiat buffers in traditional bank accounts cannot be transferred until Monday, and crypto liquidity is trapped across siloed trading entities under their intercompany arrangements.

The money exists. It just isn't available where or when it's needed.

To avoid payment delays, brokers pre-fund accounts to cover regional withdrawal spikes. They maintain weekend cash buffers. They leave liquidity sitting in wallets or accounts in case demand suddenly increases.

It's a defensive strategy. And an expensive one.

Maintaining liquidity across multiple providers and currencies comes at a cost. Capital held as a precaution in one account may be unavailable to support payment obligations elsewhere, increasing the overall funding requirements of the business.

For brokers operating across multiple markets, even relatively small inefficiencies can become significant when repeated across currencies, payment providers and legal entities.

The challenge isn't to eliminate liquidity buffers. Brokers need sufficient reserves to manage risk and meet their obligations. It is to reduce unnecessary duplication and make more effective use of the liquidity already available.

The modern broker’s solution to the cost of fragmented liquidity

Stablecoins can improve the speed and flexibility of moving funds, but the opportunity lies in how brokers manage liquidity across their entire operation.

Reducing unnecessary pre-funding, improving visibility and making more informed conversion decisions can have a much broader impact on capital efficiency.

Imagine a broker receiving stablecoin deposits on Saturday. The funds arrive almost immediately, subject to AML/CFT screening. But the broker also needs to make customer withdrawals in euros, meet obligations in dollars, and maintain sufficient liquidity across several entities.

Should it convert those stablecoins into fiat currency immediately? Hold some until later? Move liquidity to another account in anticipation of increased withdrawals?

These decisions depend on expected payment flows, available balances, foreign exchange exposure, and the cost of converting funds.

Automatically converting every stablecoin deposit into fiat may sound efficient. But it can create unnecessary transaction costs or leave the broker short of digital-asset liquidity when demand changes.

Holding everything in stablecoins creates different risks, particularly if fiat payouts are required.

Currency exposure adds another layer of complexity. A broker may receive customer deposits in dollar-denominated stablecoins while facing withdrawal obligations in euros or sterling. Converting too early can create unnecessary costs, while waiting too long can expose the business to currency movements or leave it without sufficient fiat liquidity when payouts are due.

The question isn't simply how quickly funds can be converted, but when conversion makes commercial sense within the broker's wider treasury position. The smarter approach is to treat conversion as an integral part of treasury management rather than a standalone payment function.

That means making decisions based on the company's overall liquidity position, not simply processing each incoming transaction in isolation.

From payment processing to treasury orchestration

Modern brokers are bringing these different sources of liquidity into a more connected system.

Treasury teams need unified visibility: a clear, up-to-date picture of where funds are held across bank accounts, PSPs, currencies and digital wallets.

Without that visibility, it's difficult to know whether the business genuinely needs more liquidity or simply needs to move existing funds more efficiently.

But visibility is the starting point, not the solution in itself. Knowing where funds are held doesn't automatically make them transferable.

Effective treasury management also requires the ability to act on that information: selecting appropriate conversion and settlement routes, managing liquidity across providers and operating within the regulatory and legal constraints of each entity.

The objective isn't to make every balance interchangeable. It's to give treasury teams greater control over the liquidity they can legitimately access and deploy.

Brokers need the ability to decide when to convert stablecoins, where to direct the proceeds, and how to settle payments through the appropriate banking or payment partners.

Finally, those decisions need to be connected to actual payment flows.

If a broker expects increased withdrawal demand in a particular market over the weekend, it should be able to position liquidity accordingly, subject to banking availability, regulatory requirements and entity-level restrictions.

The goal is to move away from a defensive strategy that maintains excessive reserves everywhere, towards managing liquidity dynamically as demand changes.

Balancing capital efficiency with operational resilience

Liquidity efficiency also needs to be balanced against operational resilience.

Consolidating funds with fewer providers may simplify treasury management, but excessive reliance on any single payment provider, liquidity source or settlement route can introduce new risks.

provider experiences an outage, changes its operating restrictions or temporarily suspends a payment route.

Equally, spreading funds across too many providers without a coordinated treasury strategy can create unnecessary complexity and increase the amount of capital that needs to be maintained across the business.

The challenge is to maintain sufficient diversification without creating unnecessary fragmentation.

For brokers, that means having visibility across their payment and liquidity relationships, alongside the flexibility to use alternative routes when individual providers become unavailable.

Resilience and capital efficiency shouldn't be treated as competing objectives. With the right infrastructure, brokers can maintain appropriate safeguards while improving how liquidity is allocated and managed.

What this looks like in practice

Consider a hypothetical brokerage operating across Europe, Asia and Latin America.

The business holds $5 million in operational liquidity across its payment providers, accounts and digital wallets. However, when $1 million in customer withdrawal requests arrives over the weekend, the provider responsible for those payouts has only $500,000 immediately available.

Elsewhere in the business, another provider holds $3 million, while the remaining funds are distributed across other accounts and wallets.

The brokerage has more than enough liquidity in aggregate. But that doesn't mean it can access or deploy those funds where they're needed.

Under a fragmented system, the treasury team may need to arrange additional funding, delay eligible withdrawals or maintain larger precautionary balances to avoid encountering the same problem again.

With connected treasury infrastructure, the team can assess its available balances, identify which funds are accessible and determine the most appropriate response.

Depending on the circumstances, that could mean converting stablecoins to meet fiat obligations, using an alternative settlement provider or repositioning liquidity ahead of anticipated demand.

The decision also needs to account for conversion costs, currency exposure, provider availability and any restrictions on transferring funds between legal entities.

Not every transfer will be instantaneous. Local banking hours, currency availability and legal restrictions still matter.

But better coordination can reduce unnecessary duplication of reserves and improve the use of existing capital.

The commercial benefit isn't simply faster payouts. It's the ability to meet payment obligations more efficiently without maintaining excessive liquidity across every provider and currency.

From faster payments to smarter capital management

Stablecoins have removed many of the traditional time constraints on moving value. But they haven't automatically removed the operational barriers that prevent brokers from using that value efficiently. Without connected treasury infrastructure, faster payments simply move the bottleneck elsewhere.

For brokers, competitive advantage increasingly depends on how effectively they manage liquidity across their operations: understanding where capital sits, how efficiently it can be deployed and how quickly treasury teams can respond to changing demands.

Stablecoins have changed how quickly value can move. The next challenge is building the infrastructure, controls and connectivity that allow businesses to make better use of that value.

For brokers, the real opportunity isn't simply to settle payments around the clock. It's to operate a treasury function that can keep pace.

If a broker expects increased withdrawal demand in a particular market over the weekend, it should be able to position liquidity accordingly, subject to banking availability, regulatory requirements and entity-level restrictions.

The goal is to move away from a defensive strategy that maintains excessive reserves everywhere, towards managing liquidity dynamically as demand changes.

Balancing capital efficiency with operational resilience

Liquidity efficiency also needs to be balanced against operational resilience.

Consolidating funds with fewer providers may simplify treasury management, but excessive reliance on any single payment provider, liquidity source or settlement route can introduce new risks.

provider experiences an outage, changes its operating restrictions or temporarily suspends a payment route.

Equally, spreading funds across too many providers without a coordinated treasury strategy can create unnecessary complexity and increase the amount of capital that needs to be maintained across the business.

The challenge is to maintain sufficient diversification without creating unnecessary fragmentation.

For brokers, that means having visibility across their payment and liquidity relationships, alongside the flexibility to use alternative routes when individual providers become unavailable.

Resilience and capital efficiency shouldn't be treated as competing objectives. With the right infrastructure, brokers can maintain appropriate safeguards while improving how liquidity is allocated and managed.

What this looks like in practice

Consider a hypothetical brokerage operating across Europe, Asia and Latin America.

The business holds $5 million in operational liquidity across its payment providers, accounts and digital wallets. However, when $1 million in customer withdrawal requests arrives over the weekend, the provider responsible for those payouts has only $500,000 immediately available.

Elsewhere in the business, another provider holds $3 million, while the remaining funds are distributed across other accounts and wallets.

The brokerage has more than enough liquidity in aggregate. But that doesn't mean it can access or deploy those funds where they're needed.

Under a fragmented system, the treasury team may need to arrange additional funding, delay eligible withdrawals or maintain larger precautionary balances to avoid encountering the same problem again.

With connected treasury infrastructure, the team can assess its available balances, identify which funds are accessible and determine the most appropriate response.

Depending on the circumstances, that could mean converting stablecoins to meet fiat obligations, using an alternative settlement provider or repositioning liquidity ahead of anticipated demand.

The decision also needs to account for conversion costs, currency exposure, provider availability and any restrictions on transferring funds between legal entities.

Not every transfer will be instantaneous. Local banking hours, currency availability and legal restrictions still matter.

But better coordination can reduce unnecessary duplication of reserves and improve the use of existing capital.

The commercial benefit isn't simply faster payouts. It's the ability to meet payment obligations more efficiently without maintaining excessive liquidity across every provider and currency.

From faster payments to smarter capital management

Stablecoins have removed many of the traditional time constraints on moving value. But they haven't automatically removed the operational barriers that prevent brokers from using that value efficiently. Without connected treasury infrastructure, faster payments simply move the bottleneck elsewhere.

For brokers, competitive advantage increasingly depends on how effectively they manage liquidity across their operations: understanding where capital sits, how efficiently it can be deployed and how quickly treasury teams can respond to changing demands.

Stablecoins have changed how quickly value can move. The next challenge is building the infrastructure, controls and connectivity that allow businesses to make better use of that value.

For brokers, the real opportunity isn't simply to settle payments around the clock. It's to operate a treasury function that can keep pace.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, 42 Macro CEO Darius Dale said in an interview last week his firm is waiting for signs that Bitcoin’s sell-off has run its course before buying again, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO despite an ongoing intelligence probe and OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent ICE launched a tokenized securities trading platform despite objections from dozens of major companies.

Why 42 Macro says it’s waiting to buy the Bitcoin dip

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, says his firm has trimmed its Bitcoin exposure and is waiting for signs that the sell-off has run its course before it considers buying again.

“We’ve already de-risked out of Bitcoin,” Dale said in an interview with Cointelegraph last week. “Our stress levels are low. We’re just waiting to buy.”

Dale’s comments came just days before Bitcoin fell to a two-year low around $55,100 on Saturday, raising questions about whether Bitcoin has finally found its bottom this cycle.

However, Dale warned that persistently high inflation could prompt further Fed tightening that could drain the liquidity that supports Bitcoin. The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to increase rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting on Dec. 9.

“Bitcoin doesn’t generate earnings. Bitcoin needs liquidity to go up,” he said.

Bitcoin was trading at around $64,000 at the time of the interview. Dale said it could fall another 30% to 40% if the S&P 500’s decline from its Oct. 6 peak reaches 20% by Christmas, which would put it at around $38,400. The S&P500 is currently down 7.4% from that peak.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid ongoing intelligence probe

Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and CEO after consultations with senior US government officials, concluding that his return posed no national security risk despite an ongoing investigation into an alleged foreign intelligence operation targeting him.

In a Monday announcement, Nvidia said its directors were satisfied with Huang’s candor and ability to lead following a series of discussions. The independent investigation will continue despite his reinstatement.

Nvidia shares surged 28.91% to $161.82 shortly after US markets opened on Monday, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will return to her previous role, while Harvey Jones will remain chair of the board.

The chipmaker also said it had recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprising independent directors to oversee compliance and security risks. Nvidia plans to appoint a chief compliance officer and said it would continue cooperating with government investigations.

OKX, ICE launch 113 tokenized assets despite issuer objections

OKXICE, a joint venture between cryptocurrency exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), launched a venue Monday for round-the-clock trading of tokenized US securities, with 113 assets set to roll out in stages.

The lineup includes stocks, exchange-traded funds and other exchange-traded products, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph. OKXICE named Coinbase, Circle, Fidelity Investments and Robinhood among the issuers and asset managers taking part.

Before the launch, 67 companies, including Meta, Tesla and Netflix, sought to keep tokenized versions of their shares off the venue.

Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-to-one by an underlying share, OKXICE said. Holders are entitled to dividends and voting rights where applicable.

OKXICE said the venue operates under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s Innovation Exemption. Access is limited to eligible US customers of OKX Inc., who must verify their identity, activate a self-custodial wallet and complete onboarding before trading through the OKX app.

title: Anthropic IPO: The case for a trillion-dollar valuation is taking shape
summary: A trillion-dollar valuation demands more than a convincing AI story. Anthropic's case rests on $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, more than 12 times the year-earlier figure, and $6.6 billion in positive operating cash flow. The business is growing rapidly. For investors asses...
content:
A trillion-dollar valuation demands more than a convincing AI story. Anthropic's case rests on $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, more than 12 times the year-earlier figure, and $6.6 billion in positive operating cash flow. The business is growing rapidly. For investors assessing its public debut, the harder question is whether it can grow fast enough to justify the price.

By the end of October, Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate had reached $81 billion. This measures what recent customer activity would generate over a full year, rather than revenue already earned or a forecast.

Gross margin expanded to 85.5%, while compute and infrastructure costs fell sharply as a share of revenue, suggesting that scale is improving operating efficiency. The margin reflects customer-serving costs, however, and excludes the substantial expense of developing new models.

The GAAP operating loss narrowed to $1.26 billion, while adjusted operating income turned positive at $4.08 billion. The $104 billion GAAP net loss was driven primarily by $94.3 billion of non-cash fair-value remeasurement expense; after adjustments, the company reported $5.59 billion of net income.

Anthropic remained loss-making under standard accounting measures. But revenue is now covering a much larger share of its costs, strengthening the argument that further growth could bring lasting profitability.

For traders, a stronger business doesn’t automatically mean a more attractive trade. Strong results could support further gains, but even impressive growth could disappoint if the share price already assumes more. With Exness introducing its Anthropic CFD alongside the IPO, traders can act on either assessment, taking long or short positions without owning the underlying shares.

Source: Exness FMS, Anthropic S-1 file

Enterprise adoption is broadening

Businesses are putting larger budgets behind Claude. By September 2026, nearly 12,000 businesses had each spent at least $100,000 over preceding months and more than half of the Fortune 500 had reached that threshold.

Yet spending by those Fortune 500 customers remained small relative to their overall expenses, according to Anthropic’s filing. Wider deployment could bring further growth, although the company must continue demostrating that its products justify larger budgets.

The wider market is expanding quickly too. Menlo Ventures estimates enterprise AI deployment spending reached $176.8 billion by September 2026, 5.4 times the year-earlier level. Within enterprise large-language-model APIs, Anthropic accounted for an estimated 55% of spending, compared with 31% for OpenAI and 9% for Google.

Claude has established a clear lead in this fast-growing API segment, a meaningful commercial advantage as AI usage scales.The chart shows how growth spans larger customer cohorts as well.

Source: Exness FMS, Anthropic S-1 file

Funding the next stage of growth

Generating cash from operations gives Anthropic another source of funding beyond investors and lenders. But the scale of its expansion means external capital remains important.

Anthropic also reported $131.9 billion, while the IPO and concurrent private placement added over $107 billion.

Together with operating revenue and partner funding, those resources provide a funding base for long-dated compute commitments. The liquidity position, however, doesn’t represent surplus cash. The company’s convertible notes, capital expenditure, and other obligations also make demands on those resources.

Source: Exness FMS, Anthropic S-1 file

Compute demand is extending the AI infrastructure investment cycle

The SEC filing reports approximately $900 billion in compute, infrastructure and lease commitments. The scale reflects the capacity Anthropic expects will need to train models and serve AI customers.

Long-term agreements give Anthropic access to hyperscaler and neocloud capacity while creating orders for data centers, chips, networking, and power. That supports revenue and earnings opportunities across the supply chain and can help sustain growth in US equities, particularly AI and digital infrastructure stocks.

If AI usage and revenue continue to exceed expectations, existing capacity could be absorbed faster, strengthening the economic case for another round of infrastructure investment.

But spending commitments are a bet on future demand, not proof of it. They support expansion when capacity is used profitably and become a greater burden if demand falls short.

Valuation: what future is the market pricing in?

Following its February Series G round ($380 billion post-money), Anthropic was valued at $965 billion in its May Series H round, led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia, alongside other large investors. This shows how quickly investor expectations had risen before the listing.

The November 10 IPO filing proposed $70-$78 per share; the final offer price was $83.00. By 20 Nov 2026, the shares were trading at $97.17 (official closing price), implying a valuation of around $1.27 trillion.

For context, a $1.27 trillion valuation would equal approximately 15.7 times October's $81 billion annualized revenue run rate. That is a multiple of annualized recent activity, not recorded annual revenue or earnings.

Rapid growth and improving efficiency help explain the premium investors may be willing to pay. Sustaining it requires Anthropic to keep expanding demand while turning more revenue into profit and cash.

For traders, the hurdle is higher than simply identifying a successful business. Strong results could support further gains, but even impressive growth could disappoint if the share price already assumes more.

The gap between business performance and market expectations is what CFD traders will be watching as Anthropic releases new results. Through Exness Terminal, they can follow ANT’s price movements across timeframes, analyze developing trends with indicators and drawing tools, and manage positions as the outlook changes.

Source: Exness Terminal

And before opening a trade, the Terminal’s risk calculator can calculate trade size from the trader’s selected risk amount and stop-loss level. Then the CFD trader can review and manage their open positions with the same workspace.

And when an announcement prompts rapid repricing, the broker’s pricing infrastructure comes into focus. Exness combines data from multiple sources with its own pricing algorithms, tailoring quotes and spreads to each instrument rather than simply passing through a provider’s pricing. This control supports its efforts to keep spreads competitive and pricing responsive as markets change.

Could Anthropic lift the wider AI trade?

Enterprise AI is expanding rapidly, Claude has a prominent position in APIs, revenue is scaling at extraordinary speed, gross margin is improving, and adjusted operating income has turned positive.

The sharp decline in expense ratios suggests scale is helping Anthropic absorb costs more efficiently. If revenue continues to grow faster than newly deployed capacity, that operating leverage could deepen.

Bloomberg reported that demand for Anthropic’s IPO was said to be several times the number of shares on offer, evidence of strong investor interest and a sign that the listing could rank among the market’s most sought-after AI offerings.

Could the listing help drive another leg higher in US equities on the back of AI? It could provide a powerful sentiment catalyst and a new valuation benchmark for the AI sector, potentially drawing capital back into technology, semiconductors and cloud infrastructure.

The next phase will depend on post-listing performance and evidence that Anthropic and its AI peers can generate revenue, margins and cash flow sufficient to earn attractive returns on their enormous compute investments. The IPO could energize the AI investment narrative; realized earnings will determine whether that momentum can carry the broader market further.

title: LendingUSA, Cross River Bank Debut Bitcoin-Backed Loans Up to $250K
summary: LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have launched a bitcoin-secured lending platform that allows eligible borrowers to access cash without selling their cryptocurrency.   Bitcoin Holders Can Borrow Without Selling Consumer financing company LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have launched a bitcoin-secured...
content:
LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have launched a bitcoin-secured lending platform that allows eligible borrowers to access cash without selling their cryptocurrency.

Key Takeaways

  • LendingUSA and Cross River launched a bitcoin-backed platform offering $10,000 to $250,000 loans.
  • Cross River is integrating digital assets into mainstream banking as firms expand into 30%–70% LTV loans.
  • LendingUSA and Cross River have yet to disclose interest rates, term lengths, or 2026 liquidation thresholds.

Bitcoin Holders Can Borrow Without Selling

Consumer financing company LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have launched a bitcoin-secured lending platform that allows eligible borrowers to access loans ranging from $10,000 to $250,000 without selling their cryptocurrency holdings.

Under the arrangement, borrowers pledge bitcoin as collateral and can access loans equivalent to 30%, 50%, or 70% of their pledged holdings’ value. Eligible customers can choose between interest-only payments and repayment structures that require no monthly payments.

In a statement, the companies said borrowers can repay their loans early without incurring prepayment penalties. However, eligibility depends on the value of the pledged bitcoin, the applicant’s credit history, and their ability to repay. By pledging bitcoin as collateral, borrowers can obtain financing while retaining exposure to the cryptocurrency’s potential price appreciation.

The companies’ announcement did not specify the thresholds at which borrowers could face collateral calls or forced liquidation.

“People who invest in bitcoin for the long term still have financial needs today,” said Camilo Concha, CEO of LendingUSA, in a statement. “Crypto-Secured Lending gives them another way to access funds by borrowing against their bitcoin instead of selling it.”

Concha said the company intends to use its more than a decade of consumer lending experience to simplify bitcoin-backed borrowing while offering repayment structures tailored to borrowers’ financial circumstances.

Institutional Custody and Flexible Repayment Options

Founded in 2015, LendingUSA said it has originated more than $1.5 billion in loans and served more than 200,000 borrowers. The company also maintains relationships with thousands of merchants nationwide.

The launch extends a relationship between LendingUSA and Cross River that spans more than 10 years. The companies have previously collaborated on consumer financing products, including point-of-sale loans, unsecured personal loans, and debt consolidation financing.

Under the new arrangement, Cross River will originate the bitcoin-backed loans using its existing regulated banking and lending infrastructure, while LendingUSA will facilitate the consumer-facing lending platform.

Evan L. Russo, president of Cross River, described the launch as an extension of the bank’s efforts to integrate digital assets into mainstream financial services.

“Digital assets have become a meaningful part of how many consumers build and hold wealth, and the financial system must evolve to serve them responsibly,” Russo said in a statement.

He added that the partnership reflects growing demand for financial products that allow cryptocurrency holders to access liquidity without disposing of their investments.

Meanwhile, the companies said bitcoin pledged under the program will be held by a qualified third-party custodian throughout the loan term. LendingUSA said its technology platform will emphasize transparency around loan terms, repayment obligations, and collateral requirements.

“Borrowers should understand how their loan works and feel confident navigating each step,” said Manoj Mathew, chief technology officer of LendingUSA.

Mathew said the platform is designed to simplify the application process and help borrowers understand how their bitcoin is held and managed during the loan term.

The launch comes as financial services companies explore ways to incorporate cryptocurrencies into conventional lending products. Bitcoin-backed loans allow investors to unlock liquidity without immediately selling their holdings, but borrowers remain exposed to market volatility, interest costs, and potential collateral liquidation.

Neither company disclosed the interest rates associated with the new loans, the duration of available repayment terms, or the specific collateral maintenance requirements.

title: Why 42 Macro says it’s waiting to buy the Bitcoin dip
summary: The independent macro research company warns the Bitcoin sell-off may not have yet run its course.
content:
Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, says his firm has trimmed its Bitcoin exposure and is waiting for signs that the sell-off has run its course before it considers buying again.

“We’ve already de-risked out of Bitcoin,” Dale said in an interview with Cointelegraph last week. “Our stress levels are low. We’re just waiting to buy.”

Dale’s comments came just days before Bitcoin fell to a two-year low around $55,100 on Saturday, raising questions about whether Bitcoin has finally found its bottom this cycle.

However, Dale warned that persistently high inflation could prompt further Fed tightening that could drain the liquidity that supports Bitcoin. The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to increase rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting on Dec. 9.

“Bitcoin doesn’t generate earnings. Bitcoin needs liquidity to go up,” he said.

Bitcoin was trading at around $64,000 at the time of the interview. Dale said it could fall another 30% to 40% if the S&P 500’s decline from its Oct. 6 peak reaches 20% by Christmas, which would put it at around $38,400. The S&P500 is currently down 7.4% from that peak.

Related: Bitcoin rebounds 17% from $55K lows as Nvidia rally sparks $500M crypto liquidations

Asked when 42 Macro may consider buying Bitcoin again, Dale said the firm will be looking at its own market signals.

“And once we pivot to a risk on market regime, once Bitcoin, the bottoming process concludes and our signals go from bearish right now to neutral or maybe even back to bullish. That’s when you want to buy.”

42 Macro sees a Fed pivot lifting Bitcoin in 2027

Despite near-term caution, Dale expects the conditions to become more favorable for Bitcoin around the middle of 2027, when easing inflation could give the Fed room to shift away from tighter monetary policy.

“So we think 2027 will be a phenomenal year for stocks, gold, Bitcoin,” he said.

Dale said the Fed may need to see second-quarter inflation data before changing course, putting the potential shift in late June or in the first half of the third quarter.

title: Fortitude Clears Key Vote on Path to Nasdaq Zcash Mining Debut
summary: Fortitude Mining is moving closer to a Nasdaq debut after Heartsciences shareholders approved their merger with 86% support. The development comes as Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi makes a case for zcash as protection against bitcoin’s potential security risks. Heartsciences Backs Fortitude Merger A Nas...
content:
Fortitude Mining is moving closer to a Nasdaq debut after Heartsciences shareholders approved their merger with 86% support. The development comes as Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi makes a case for zcash as protection against bitcoin’s potential security risks.

Key Takeaways

  • HeartSciences shareholders backed the Fortitude merger with 86% support.
  • Fortitude brings 60+ MW of zcash mining power to public markets.
  • Haseeb Qureshi sees zcash as insurance against potential long-term bitcoin security risks.

Heartsciences Backs Fortitude Merger

A Nasdaq-listed medical technology company is preparing to become a gateway for Wall Street investors seeking exposure to zcash mining.

Heartsciences shareholders approved a merger with Fortitude Mining Holdings, a subsidiary of Digital Currency Group (DCG), at a November 19 meeting. Approximately 86% of votes supported the transaction, clearing a major hurdle in Fortitude’s push into public markets.

The combined company will operate as Fortitude Mining Group, with shares expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker TUDE. The transaction still requires Nasdaq approval and other closing conditions.

Fortitude Brings 60 MW of Zcash Mining Power to Wall Street

Fortitude enters the proposed merger with substantial infrastructure.

The company controls more than 60 megawatts of power capacity across seven facilities in New York, South Dakota, Nebraska and Texas. Its zcash mining operations generate over 5.4 GSol/s of computing power.

Fortitude says its integrated operations, including power contracts and equipment maintenance, allow it to mine ZEC below market prices.

“Today’s vote paves the way for Fortitude to become a premier publicly traded zcash mining platform,” said CEO Jaime Leverton.

Under the merger terms, Fortitude expects to contribute $2 million in ZEC tokens at closing, potentially supplied by DCG. The listing would give traditional investors access to zcash mining through regulated public equities without directly purchasing crypto assets.

Dragonfly Partner Calls Zcash ‘Insurance for Bitcoin’

The development coincides with renewed debate over Zcash’s role in the broader crypto ecosystem.

Speaking on the When Shift Happens podcast, Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi described Zcash as a potential hedge against bitcoin’s long-term vulnerabilities.

“Zcash has already decided what they’re going to do if there is a foundational break in public-key cryptography. The amount of zcash you want to hold relative to bitcoin is responsive to the level of risk. It’s an insurance policy,” Qureshi said.

He argued that rapid advances in artificial intelligence and mathematics could eventually challenge existing cryptographic systems, potentially forcing major blockchain upgrades.

Qureshi believes bitcoin could struggle to adapt quickly enough, while zcash has already outlined a response.

Those concerns remain hypothetical, but they underscore growing interest in privacy-focused cryptocurrencies as Fortitude prepares to bring zcash mining into the public equity market.

title: Robert Kiyosaki Renews Bitcoin Case, Warns of Economic Crash Worse Than 2008
summary: Robert Kiyosaki renewed his case for owning bitcoin and ether directly, warning that a downturn could surpass the 2008 financial crisis. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author raised the possibility of a global depression. Kiyosaki Revisits His Case for Direct Ownership Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poo...
content:
Robert Kiyosaki renewed his case for owning bitcoin and ether directly, warning that a downturn could surpass the 2008 financial crisis. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author raised the possibility of a global depression.

Key Takeaways

  • Robert Kiyosaki warned that the current downturn could be worse than the 2008 crisis.
  • He reaffirmed his preference for buying bitcoin and ether directly.
  • Treasury data put U.S. debt at $40.71 trillion on Nov. 19.

Kiyosaki Revisits His Case for Direct Ownership

Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad, reiterated on Nov. 22 that he was buying bitcoin, ether, gold, and silver directly, without exchange-traded funds (ETFs). He tied his case for direct ownership to concerns about Federal Reserve policy, U.S. debt, and the risk of a financial crisis.

He wrote on X:

“This crash we are just now sliding into is much bigger than 2008. Possibly a global depression.”

The position echoes his earlier objections to bitcoin ETFs. In April 2024, he said he preferred owning assets directly and wanted to stay away from Wall Street products for his own portfolio. His latest list also included real estate and oil.

Kiyosaki grouped bitcoin with gold and silver as assets he expects to benefit if his forecast proves right. The comparison between bitcoin and gold comes with different supply constraints. Bitcoin’s issuance follows a schedule with a 21 million cap, while gold supply grows through mining.

What His 2008 Comparison Relies On

The famous author pointed to mortgage-linked derivatives and Lehman Brothers’ failure in 2008 to explain his warning. An essay on Federal Reserve History, a website run by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, traces the roots of the subprime crisis to an expansion of high-risk mortgage lending and rising home prices. Falling prices then made refinancing harder as defaults mounted.

Kiyosaki said the derivatives market is measured in quadrillions, or thousands of trillions. The Bank for International Settlements’ global derivatives market data put outstanding over-the-counter contracts at $846 trillion in notional value in June 2025. Their gross market value, which measures the cost of replacing contracts at prevailing prices, was $21.8 trillion.

He linked his buying to expectations of more money creation and put U.S. debt at $49 trillion. The Treasury’s total public debt figures showed $40.71 trillion outstanding on Nov. 19, including $32.90 trillion held by the public and $7.81 trillion in intragovernmental holdings.

Bitcoin Slides Back After Topping $64,000

The renewed case for direct ownership followed several comments about when to buy. On Nov. 4, he described purchases during the sell-off, saying he had added bitcoin, gold, and silver while others panicked. He linked those purchases to rising debt and concerns about government-issued money.

On Nov. 20, his advice on timing purchases emphasized waiting for a bottom. He recalled buying bitcoin at $20,000 after an earlier downturn and said he intended to wait for another bottom before buying again.

Bitcoin rebounded from a weekend low near $55,600, but the recovery lost momentum on Nov. 23. After topping $64,000, it pulled back below $61,000. By 5:34 p.m. EST, bitcoin had edged up to $61,128, still down 5.78% over seven days, Bitcoin.com Markets data showed.

title: Google wants to make you the star of your own AI slop movies
summary: Viewers could find their AI-doppelgangers inserted into the crowd during the Cricket World Cup, or take a leading role in their very own romantic comedy.
content:
Google has filed for a patent on a system that uses information it has on you to create a customized AI-generated TV channel, full of shows that star you as the protagonist.

The patent, submitted May 13, 2025, and published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on Thursday, describes a system called “My Channel,” filled with AI-generated content tailored to a user’s watch history and demographic data. The system could use photos or videos of the viewer to create a digital likeness and generate a synthetic voice for their character’s dialogue.

“You are a customized video generating model. Generate a customized video for a user where the user will play the protagonist,” the example AI prompt reads.

“The generated customized video includes characteristics based on the <user_profile>. The generated customized video follows the style and format of the <top_watches> of the user. The generated customized video sticks to the <preferred_genres> of the user, but the narrative for the generated customized video is customized.”

Many companies file patents that never become products. However, Google’s proposal isn’t too far off from reality. In China, AI-powered filmmakers are generating hundreds of one-minute TV microdramas, called “duanju,” each day.

Related: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid ongoing intelligence probe

Shortical, an Israeli-based streaming service available in the US, produces fully AI-generated microdramas among conventional titles. It even allows users to audition their face to be potentially added as characters in future AI-generated microseries.

Google envisions the kinds of genres a user could find themselves starring in. Source: USPTO

In another example, Google describes a user who has recently watched a video about a cricket player in the Cricket World Cup.

“The video should incorporate elements of the Cricket World Cup and Player 1’s recent performance. Perhaps [user_name] could be cheering for India in the stands or interacting with Player 1 in some way,” it wrote.

Google’s proposal also makes room for commercials. In one version described in the filing, when a viewer picks an AI-generated show, an ad server retrieves the video, inserts ads and streams the resulting version to the viewer’s TV.

The application names Aravind Reddy Ayuluri, a software engineer and Prameela Kavya Thummuru, a machine learning engineer at Google as the inventors.

Cointelegraph reached out to Google for comment.

title: ‘The Mistake Has Been Corrected’: Musk, Trump, CZ React to Nvidia’s CEO Reversal
summary: Elon Musk, President Donald Trump, and Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao welcomed Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chuck Schumer challenged the decision as investigations and questions about U.S. export controls remain unresolved. Elon Musk Welcomes Huang’s Return t...
content:
Elon Musk, President Donald Trump, and Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao welcomed Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chuck Schumer challenged the decision as investigations and questions about U.S. export controls remain unresolved.

Key Takeaways

  • Elon Musk called Jensen Huang’s reinstatement a correction to Nvidia’s earlier decision.
  • President Donald Trump and Binance founder CZ welcomed the CEO’s return after his resignation.
  • Senators Warren and Schumer pressed for scrutiny of Nvidia and government involvement.

Elon Musk Welcomes Huang’s Return to Nvidia

Tesla and Spacex CEO Elon Musk welcomed Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia (Nasdaq: NVDA) on Nov. 23 after the chipmaker’s board reinstated its founder as president, CEO, and director. The unanimous vote reversed Huang’s departure 11 days earlier and brought him back to the company while an independent investigation remains open.

Musk commented on Nvidia’s decision on X, writing:

“The mistake has been corrected.”

The Nvidia board said discussions with Huang satisfied directors about his candor and ability to lead. It cited input from senior levels of the U.S. government in concluding that his return posed no national security risk, but said the inquiry into a reported foreign intelligence effort targeting him would continue.

Musk had previously backed a petition seeking Huang’s reinstatement. The campaign’s updated tally as of Nov. 23 shows 206,428 names: 10,348 self-identified current employees, 1,841 former employees, 108,079 shareholders, and 86,160 other supporters. Those affiliations were self-reported and unverified. Musk had warned that Huang’s exit could jeopardize supply-chain arrangements.

Trump and CZ Applaud the Reversal

President Donald Trump endorsed the board’s decision in a statement supporting Huang’s return on Nov. 23. The president declared:

“The Nvidia Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… Congratulations to Jensen, the Nvidia Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World!”

Trump stated that the U.S. government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security risk. He also urged Nvidia to continue examining its compliance with U.S. export controls. The company’s new National Security and Export Control Committee will oversee trade compliance and related risks.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, known as CZ, welcomed Huang back. He posted on X:

“Glad to see @JensenHuang back. 👏”

Zhao had called Huang’s departure a mistake for Nvidia on Nov. 12. The company had appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO during his absence; she continues in her finance role. Board Chair Harvey C. Jones remains chair.

Senators Press for Answers as Bitcoin Reacts

U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Huang’s return reckless and demanded answers about Nvidia’s export control compliance and the government’s input into the board’s decision. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said Democrats would investigate potential wrongdoing and continue pursuing policies to restrict the flow of advanced U.S. technology to adversaries.

Warren added:

“Huang’s return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.”

Huang’s reinstatement coincided with a rebound in bitcoin and crypto-linked stocks. Bitcoin hit an intraday high of $64,505 at 9:29 a.m. ET after a weekend decline near $55,000, while shares of several bitcoin miners rose sharply. The bitcoin price response to Huang’s return came amid wider gains in technology shares.

BTC surrendered most of its post-announcement rally by early evening, trading at $61,128 at 5:34 p.m. ET, up 0.59% over 24 hours. The price was still down 5.78% over the past week and 23.88% over the past month.

Bitcoin’s price reflects broader market sentiment and liquidity, among other forces. Nvidia’s board said its independent investigation would proceed to a conclusion, and the company is searching for a chief compliance officer to oversee its compliance work.

title: Visa Launches Wallet That Lets AI Agents Earn Stablecoins for Owners
summary: Visa has opened an experimental wallet that lets eligible U.S. users verify AI agents with a payment card and pursue paid tasks. Rewards arrive in dollar-backed stablecoin OUSD when a task requester accepts the agent’s work. Visa Opens Agent Wallet for Paid Work Visa (NYSE: V) introduced a new versi...
content:
Visa has opened an experimental wallet that lets eligible U.S. users verify AI agents with a payment card and pursue paid tasks. Rewards arrive in dollar-backed stablecoin OUSD when a task requester accepts the agent’s work.

Key Takeaways

  • Eligible U.S. users can verify agents with a Visa card.
  • Accepted tasks pay OUSD into the owner’s wallet.
  • Visa screens tasks before agents see them but does not judge the work.

Visa Opens Agent Wallet for Paid Work

Visa (NYSE: V) introduced a new version of its Visa CLI agent wallet through Visa Crypto Labs on Nov. 22, allowing eligible U.S. cardholders to verify AI agents and connect them to paid tasks. Cuy Sheffield, head of Visa Crypto Labs, described the experimental wallet launch on X.

Sheffield wrote:

“At Visa Crypto Labs, we believe ordinary people should be able to earn income from the AI economy.”

Users connect an agent and verify ownership using an eligible Visa card. According to the Visa CLI card requirements, a bank confirms the card with a one-time code before Visa creates a signing key for the agent. The card serves as a verification credential; agents pay in Open USD (OUSD), a dollar-pegged stablecoin on the Tempo blockchain, from the owner’s wallet rather than charging the card.

The service requires an approved account and currently accepts supported U.S. personal Visa cards. Prepaid and corporate cards are excluded, as are cards from banks that cannot complete the check. Visa’s current product status says task payouts and wallet balances use real OUSD on Tempo.

How Verified Agents Find Tasks

Through Taskmarket, agents can search for assignments, complete work and submit it for review. Visa’s paid task instructions state that requesters pay rewards to the owner’s wallet after accepting a submission. A completed task alone does not establish that a payment has been made.

Some assignments require a verified worker. Taskmarket’s agent verification rules describe how a signing key identifies an agent when it claims or submits work on Tempo. Visa says newly connected agents’ keys are registered in its Agent Directory; agents connected before Nov. 18 retain sandbox listings.

Owners normally approve each step, including claiming a task and submitting work. An optional setting lets agents running on a user’s computer take certain screened actions without individual approval, while settling a task still requires consent. Visa screens task instructions before agents see them and again before signing or payment.

A submission fee may apply after a task’s free entries are exhausted. If a requester misses the review deadline, then the agent can request settlement, which the owner must approve. Visa’s controls do not assess the quality of an agent’s work.

OUSD Payments and Visa’s Broader Wallet Plans

Visa was among the founding partners when OUSD launched across four blockchains in September. Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, and Stripe joined Visa in committing more than $1 billion, and the token went live natively on Ethereum, Base, Solana, and Tempo.

Dollar-pegged tokens aim to track a fixed value, usually $1, but their price can vary. The mechanics of dollar-backed stablecoins depend on reserves and redemption access. Owners can send OUSD out of their Visa CLI wallet to a withdrawal address.

Visa has developed a distinct stablecoin platform for institutions, offering banks and payment providers wallet and settlement tools. Its new agent wallet instead links individual card verification to software that can seek paid work.

The rollout follows Visa’s involvement in OpenAI’s ChatGPT Wallet launch, which lets agents make card purchases after user approval. Visa CLI adds a way for agents to receive OUSD for accepted work, with each owner able to connect up to 25 agents under the current rules.

title: Ethereum Foundation doubles protocol security team ahead of overhaul
summary: The foundation said its next upgrade will be harder than the Merge, and the required pace of development will make it easier to ship bugs.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 24, 2026

The foundation said its next upgrade will be harder than the Merge, and the required pace of development will make it easier to ship bugs.

The Ethereum Foundation says it has doubled its protocol security team as it accelerates work to overhaul Ethereum’s defenses against threats posed by quantum computers and artificial intelligence.

In a Monday blog post, Ethereum Foundation researcher Kev Wedderburn said that while Ethereum has been planning ways to mitigate threats posed by quantum computers, AI has now emerged as a more urgent risk.

The planned overhaul would change how Ethereum validators sign messages, how users authorize transactions and how Ethereum verifies data posted by rollups.

“This upgrade is harder than the Merge, and we have less time,” said Wedderburn, while acknowledging that faster development “makes it easier to ship bugs.”

He said in response, the foundation has expanded its protocol security team to ensure formal verification and security work can keep pace with development.

“Every layer of the protocol and ecosystem will need to adapt to the reality that hardening the protocol is now our highest priority,” he added.

Earlier this month, Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake outlined a December 2028 target for completing Ethereum’s post-quantum and post-AI transition, a year earlier than the foundation’s previously announced quantum-resistance deadline.
