title: Solana Price Prediction 2030: Is $2,000 SOL Still on the Table After a 75% Crash?
summary: Key takeaways SOL trades near $73, roughly 75% below its January 2025 high of $294, and tracked Binance whale positioning leans bearish (about 20% longs) while around 79% of broader accounts are long. PumpGlass shows a $19.5 million short-liquidation cluster near $79.01 and long-liquidation clusters...
content:
Key takeaways

  • SOL trades near $73, roughly 75% below its January 2025 high of $294, and tracked Binance whale positioning leans bearish (about 20% longs) while around 79% of broader accounts are long.
  • PumpGlass shows a $19.5 million short-liquidation cluster near $79.01 and long-liquidation clusters near $69.39 and $68.01.
  • Bitwise’s $385 base case depends on tokenized-stock trading, and a $2,000 SOL would imply about $1.38 trillion in total-supply value under NewsBTC’s 690 million-token assumption.
  • NewsBTC’s conditional 2030 scenarios are bearish $40–$110, base $180–$400, bullish $600–$1,000 and extreme upside $1,500–$2,000+.

Solana has lost roughly 75% of its value since reaching an all-time high of $294 in January 2025. Large futures traders are leaning bearish, yet institutional analysts continue to see a future in which SOL trades at four digit prices. So, how realistic is a $2,000 Solana price prediction for 2030?

At around $73, SOL is trading at a fraction of the price some of Wall Street’s most optimistic forecasts suggest it could eventually reach. But a steep discount to an analyst’s target does not necessarily make an asset cheap.

NewsBTC examined liquidation heatmaps, whale positions, historical price action, network economics and institutional valuation models to understand where Solana stands today and what it could realistically be worth by the end of the decade.

The findings paint a more complicated picture than either bulls or bears might expect.

Solana Whales Are Betting Against the Crowd

Perhaps the most interesting signal right now comes from the derivatives market.

According to a November 23 snapshot from PumpGlass, only around 20% of the tracked Binance whale position value was allocated to longs. Meanwhile, approximately 79% of the broader trader accounts were positioned long.

Although the two figures measure different aspects of market positioning, the divergence is striking. Large traders appear considerably less optimistic than the wider trading crowd.

The average entry price of tracked whale shorts stood near $77.63, compared with $77.05 for whale longs. With SOL trading around $73 at the time of observation, the short side was better positioned.

Binance whale and trader positioning for SOL. Source: PumpGlass, November 23, 2026.

The on-chain picture offers another reason for caution.

On November 19, blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that two large holders had unstaked a combined 2.31 million SOL worth approximately $169.4 million before transferring the tokens to Coinbase Prime-associated addresses.

Exchange deposits do not necessarily mean those tokens were sold. Institutional investors use custody platforms for several purposes, including collateral management and portfolio rebalancing. Still, the movement is worth monitoring.

What matters now is whether large holders begin accumulating again or whether the recent decline has further to run.

A $19.5 Million Liquidation Cluster Could Influence SOL’s Next Move

Solana’s liquidation heatmap reveals an interesting battle developing around its current trading range.

PumpGlass identified several concentrations of potentially vulnerable leveraged positions in its November 23, 19:22 UTC observation.

Price level Estimated liquidation exposure
$79.01 $19.5 million in shorts
$69.39 $10.7 million in longs
$68.01 $15.1 million in longs

SOLUSDT seven-day liquidation heatmap. Source: PumpGlass, November 23, 2026. Modeled estimates, not guaranteed orders.

A recovery toward $79 could put considerable pressure on short sellers. Conversely, a breakdown below $69 could expose another wave of leveraged longs to forced closures.

Data from CoinGlass adds another layer to the picture. At 21:31 UTC on November 23, Solana’s futures open interest stood at $3.86 billion, while rolling 24-hour liquidations reached approximately $30.59 million. Shorts accounted for roughly 72% of those liquidations.

SOL had gained around 3.1% over the same rolling period.

The recovery is consistent with some bearish positions being forced out of the market. However, a liquidated short is not the same as a new investor buying SOL for the next four years.

Until stronger spot demand emerges, traders should be careful about interpreting a short squeeze as the beginning of a sustainable recovery.

Liquidation concentrations are modeled estimates, not guaranteed future orders, and can change considerably as traders adjust their positions.

Solana Technical Analysis: The Levels That Could Change Everything

Solana’s price structure has deteriorated considerably since its September recovery.

After closing July near $72.79, SOL climbed to $103 in August and $117.99 in September. The recovery subsequently unraveled, with October closing near $95.35 before prices returned to the low $70s in November.

Solana (SOL) price chart, 2026. Source: Binance SOLUSDT, TradingView.

Looking at SOL’s historical price action on Binance, using the TradingView SOLUSDT market as the chart reference, five key price regions stand out:

SOL price Technical significance
$60–$65 Major downside reference
$69–$71 Immediate support
$75–$80 short term resistance
$88–$95 Intermediate recovery zone
$100–$118 Broader trend recovery territory

The daily Relative Strength Index was in the low 30s in the observed CoinGlass data, suggesting weak momentum and proximity to oversold territory.

But oversold markets can remain oversold.

A sustained recovery above $80 would be the first encouraging development. Reclaiming $95 and subsequently $100 would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control.

On the downside, failure to hold the $65 range would bring Solana’s 2026 low near $60.42 back into focus.

Our technical assessment remains cautious. There is room for a meaningful relief rally, particularly given the nearby short-liquidation exposure, but the broader market structure has yet to establish a convincing reversal.

The $73 Token Behind a Multibillion-Dollar Economy

While Solana’s price has struggled, its blockchain continues to facilitate substantial financial activity.

According to DefiLlama, Solana’s November 23 network metrics included:

Network metric Reported value
DeFi total value locked $4.68 billion
Stablecoin market capitalization $13.14 billion
Daily DEX trading volume $1.12 billion
Daily active addresses 1.8 million
Daily transactions 83.42 million
Daily application revenue $2.07 million
Daily chain revenue $23,978

There is something particularly interesting about those last two figures.

Applications running on Solana generated considerably more revenue than the chain itself under DefiLlama’s respective measurement definitions.

This highlights what could become Solana’s biggest valuation challenge.

A blockchain can attract substantial activity and billions of dollars in trading volume without its native token capturing a proportional share of that economic value.

Cheap transactions are excellent for adoption. Whether they are equally good for SOL’s valuation is another question entirely.

That is why Solana’s expansion beyond speculative trading could prove so important.

The blockchain’s growing presence in stablecoins, payments and tokenized real-world assets opens the door to financial activity that could persist even when speculative markets cool.

Its infrastructure is also evolving. The Solana Foundation reported the activation of Alpenglow in October 2026, targeting transaction finality near 150 milliseconds. November’s introduction of Solana 1.0 marked another milestone in the network’s development.

Meanwhile, the announced integration with DTCC’s Tokenization Service, expected in the second half of 2027, could represent a meaningful institutional opportunity.

The real test will be how much financial activity these developments ultimately bring onchain, and how much value SOL captures from it.

Wall Street’s Solana Price Predictions Are Surprisingly Far Apart

Institutional research offers a glimpse into how differently analysts view Solana’s future.

Research firm Bear case Base case Bull case / reported target Horizon
VanEck $9.81 $334.70 $3,211.28 2030
Standard Chartered Not disclosed Not disclosed $2,000 target 2030
Bitwise $80 $385 $1,100 2031

VanEck’s October 2023 research produced one of the widest forecast ranges, with its most optimistic scenario placing SOL above $3,200.

Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick was reported in February 2026 to have projected a $2,000 Solana price by 2030, partly based on the network’s potential in stablecoin micropayments.

However, the bank’s reported $250 end-of-2026 target looks increasingly difficult to achieve from current levels. Its original research note was not available for independent review.

Perhaps the most interesting analysis comes from Bitwise’s November 2026 research, which connects Solana’s future valuation to tokenized stock trading.

The asset manager’s base case assumes Solana captures 50% of tokenized-stock trading volume in 2031, generating approximately $6.75 billion in annual network economic value.

Applying a 40-times valuation multiple produces an estimated SOL price of $385, based on a projected total supply of 700 million tokens.

The report acknowledges the key dependency:

“

Most of the price increase depends on how quickly stocks move onchain.

In its bullish scenario, Solana captures 65% of tokenized-stock trading, generating approximately $12.83 billion in network economic value and supporting a modeled price of $1,100.

These assumptions reveal just how much needs to go right before four-digit SOL prices become fundamentally convincing.

The $1.38 Trillion Problem With a $2,000 Solana

Here is something many price predictions overlook: Solana’s token supply will not necessarily remain where it is today.

Unlike Bitcoin, SOL has no fixed maximum supply. Its inflationary issuance framework rewards validators and staking participants, while future governance decisions can influence the rate of supply growth.

With around 592 million SOL currently circulating, we use an illustrative assumption of 690 million total tokens by 2030 for our valuation scenarios.

The numbers put popular price targets into perspective.

SOL price in 2030 Implied total-supply valuation
$100 $69 billion
$300 $207 billion
$500 $345 billion
$1,000 $690 billion
$1,500 $1.035 trillion
$2,000 $1.38 trillion
$3,000 $2.07 trillion

These are total-supply valuations rather than projected circulating market capitalizations.

At $2,000, Solana would need to command a valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion under our assumptions.

Using Bitwise’s base-case valuation multiple of 40 times annual network economic value as an illustrative benchmark, Solana would need to generate approximately $34.5 billion in annual economic value to support that figure.

Even at a more generous 60-times multiple, the requirement would be $23 billion annually.

That is substantially more demanding than simply attracting another wave of cryptocurrency traders.

Our Solana Price Prediction for 2030

Based on the network’s economic opportunity, competitive landscape, token supply and institutional research, NewsBTC has developed four conditional valuation scenarios.

NewsBTC original analysis: conditional SOL price scenarios for 2030. Editorial scenarios, not statistical forecasts.

Scenario SOL price in 2030 Implied total-supply value
Bearish $40–$110 $28B–$76B
Base case $180–$400 $124B–$276B
Bullish $600–$1,000 $414B–$690B
Extreme upside $1,500–$2,000+ $1.04T–$1.38T+

These ranges are conditional editorial scenarios, not statistically derived forecasts. Outcomes outside these ranges, including substantially greater losses, are possible.

Bearish Scenario: $40–$110

Solana remains relevant but struggles to turn network adoption into meaningful economic value for SOL. Institutional projects develop more slowly than expected, competitors gain market share, and speculative trading remains an important source of demand.

Solana does not need to fail for this scenario to materialize. It only needs to fall short of the expectations investors have placed on it.

Base Scenario: $180–$400

Our central expectation assumes Solana retains its position among the leading smart-contract networks while expanding its role in payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets.

Under this scenario, the network does not need to dominate global finance. It needs to establish a durable position within it and capture more economic value from the applications it supports.

Bullish Scenario: $600–$1,000

Solana becomes a major platform for tokenized equities, stablecoin settlements and high-frequency financial applications.

Institutional adoption moves beyond announcements, network revenue expands significantly, and the broader cryptocurrency market benefits from favorable liquidity conditions.

At $1,000, SOL would trade at approximately 13.8 times its November 23 reference price.

Extreme Scenario: $1,500–$2,000+

This is where the most ambitious institutional predictions become conceivable.

Solana would need to capture a significant share of a much larger on-chain financial economy, scale its infrastructure accordingly, and translate that activity into sustained demand for SOL.

An exceptional cryptocurrency bull market could also temporarily push valuations beyond what underlying economics justify.

We would not consider this the most likely outcome based on today’s evidence.

The Five Signals That Could Make Us Raise Our Forecast

Rather than following every new price target, long-term SOL investors may benefit from monitoring five developments:

  • Stablecoin adoption: Growth in recurring payment and settlement activity beyond speculative trading.
  • Institutional tokenization: Actual financial instruments and trading volumes going live on Solana.
  • Network economics: Sustained growth in fees, economic value and demand for SOL.
  • Institutional capital: Persistent ETF inflows and broader spot-market participation.
  • Technical resilience: Reliable performance under heavy demand without sacrificing security or decentralization.

Competition from Ethereum, its scaling ecosystem and specialized financial networks remains a considerable risk.

If Solana’s transaction volumes rise while the economic value captured by the network stagnates, we would have reason to lower our valuation assumptions, regardless of how impressive the adoption statistics look.

Is Solana Undervalued at $73?

The current market offers an interesting contradiction.

Solana’s blockchain has established a meaningful financial ecosystem, yet its token is trading roughly 75% below its historical record. Large futures traders are cautious, while institutional research continues to outline substantial long-term opportunities.

Our $180 to $400 base-case range for 2030 reflects the possibility that Solana can grow without fulfilling every ambitious expectation placed on it.

A move toward $1,000 is conceivable under considerably stronger conditions. At $2,000, however, investors would be betting on Solana becoming one of the world’s most valuable digital financial networks.

The opportunity is there. The evidence that would justify such a valuation is not there yet.

For now, the most interesting question surrounding Solana is not how many transactions it can process, but how much those transactions will eventually be worth to SOL holders.

Solana Price Prediction 2030: Frequently Asked Questions

How much will Solana be worth in 2030?

NewsBTC’s analysis places Solana between $180 and $400 by 2030 under our base-case scenario. Strong institutional adoption and improved network economics could support a bullish range of $600 to $1,000, while weaker growth could leave SOL trading between $40 and $110.

Can Solana reach $500 by 2030?

Solana could reach $500 by 2030 if its adoption across payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets continues to expand. Based on an assumed total supply of 690 million SOL, a $500 price would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $345 billion.

Can Solana reach $1,000 by 2030?

A $1,000 Solana price is possible under a strong bullish scenario. However, achieving and sustaining that valuation would require substantial institutional adoption, higher network economic value and favorable cryptocurrency market conditions. At $1,000, Solana’s implied total-supply valuation would reach approximately $690 billion.

Can Solana reach $2,000 by 2030?

Standard Chartered was reported to have projected a $2,000 SOL price by 2030 in February 2026. However, our analysis considers this an extreme bullish scenario. Reaching $2,000 would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion, requiring extraordinary growth in Solana’s financial ecosystem and demand for SOL.

Can Solana reach $10,000?

While mathematically possible, a $10,000 SOL price would imply a valuation of approximately $6.9 trillion based on our 2030 supply assumption. There is currently insufficient economic evidence to support such a valuation within this timeframe.

Is Solana a good investment for the next five years?

Solana offers long-term exposure to decentralized finance, stablecoin payments and institutional asset tokenization. However, its investment potential depends on whether growing network adoption translates into sustainable demand for SOL. Competition, token inflation, market volatility and regulatory developments remain significant risks.

Will Solana overtake Ethereum by 2030?

Solana could challenge Ethereum in areas such as decentralized trading, payments and financial applications. However, overtaking Ethereum by market capitalization would require substantial growth in Solana’s economic value, institutional demand and developer ecosystem. Higher transaction volumes alone would not guarantee that outcome.

What are analysts predicting for Solana in 2030?

VanEck’s October 2023 research placed SOL at $334.70 in its base case and $3,211.28 in its most optimistic scenario for 2030. Standard Chartered was reported to have projected $2,000 in February 2026, while Bitwise’s November 2026 research estimated a base-case price of $385 and a bullish price of $1,100 for 2031.

What could cause Solana’s price to fall further?

Weak spot demand, large-holder selling, leveraged liquidations, network disruptions and deteriorating global liquidity could all contribute to further declines. From a technical perspective, losing the $60 to $65 support region identified in our November 23, 2026 analysis would significantly weaken the recovery outlook.

title: Clockwork Laundering: Binance Hackers Follow a Daily Cadence Linked to China
summary: The laundering operation tied to Binance’s $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft remains active to this very day, with stolen funds continuing to move onchain even after large-scale ether (ETH) swaps temporarily came to a halt. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reports that at least $247 million in sto...
content:
The laundering operation tied to Binance’s $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft remains active to this very day, with stolen funds continuing to move onchain even after large-scale ether (ETH) swaps temporarily came to a halt. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reports that at least $247 million in stolen bitcoin (BTC) has entered coinjoins.

Key Takeaways

  • Ether-to-bitcoin swaps paused for two days beginning Nov. 21, but the movement of stolen bitcoin through privacy-enhancing transactions continued.
  • Elliptic identified at least 3,930 BTC, worth $247 million, entering coinjoins, with nearly all the activity coordinated through Kruw.
  • Elliptic’s chief scientist suspects Chinese laundering networks may be involved, although transaction timing alone cannot establish their identities or locations.

Ethereum Swaps Stall While Bitcoin Mixing Accelerates

The machinery behind one of cryptocurrency’s largest thefts appears to operate on separate schedules. While the conversion of stolen ETH into BTC temporarily stopped, another component of the operation continued processing funds through transactions designed to complicate blockchain tracing.

As Bitcoin.com News recently reported, Elliptic disclosed last week that the hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion digital asset theft moved approximately $860 million in stolen ether between Nov. 17 and 20, redistributing 488,000 ETH across smaller wallets as part of an elaborate laundering operation.

During that period, the perpetrators reportedly converted roughly $70 million worth of ether into BTC, setting the stage for another round of transactions designed to obscure the stolen funds’ origins. Three days later, according to Elliptic’s Nov. 23 update, the ether swaps continued until 6:28 a.m. UTC on Nov. 21, when approximately 5,900 ETH had been exchanged that day.

Activity then stopped for two days before restarting on Monday morning. During the interruption, four remaining large ethereum addresses were left untouched, while approximately 425,000 ETH awaited conversion in previously prepared batches.

By 9 a.m. UTC on Nov. 23, Elliptic says another 41,000 ETH had entered the decentralized exchange (DEX) and cross-chain liquidity platform Thorchain. Since Nov. 17, approximately 58,000 ETH, valued at $100 million, had been exchanged for roughly 1,630 BTC. Yet the interruption did little to restrain the bitcoin mixing operation.

Elliptic documented approximately 580 BTC entering coinjoins on Nov. 22, followed by another 350 BTC on Nov. 23. The cumulative amount reached at least 3,930 BTC, worth approximately $247 million, since Nov. 1. Basically, a coinjoin combines bitcoin from multiple participants into a single transaction, making it considerably harder to establish which outgoing coins belong to any particular participant.

Kruw Coordination

Elliptic emphasized that its calculations represent minimum amounts because previously mixed bitcoin can undergo additional rounds without increasing the initial tally. The firm’s analysis attributes approximately 40% of the mixed bitcoin to converted ether holdings, another 40% to XRP, 17% to SOL, and the remainder primarily to TRX.

Bitcoin.com News noted on Friday that nearly all the BTC mixing transactions were coordinated by Kruw, a coordinator commonly used by Wasabi Wallet participants. Coordinators arrange transactions among participants without taking custody of their bitcoin. Kruw operates as an independent, third-party coinjoin coordinator primarily serving Wasabi Wallet users and other compatible privacy clients.

Following the shutdown of Wasabi’s official coordinator in mid-2024, Wasabi Wallet adopted a model that allows users to select independent, community-operated coordinators. Kruw subsequently emerged as the network’s most widely used coordinator, organizing coinjoin transactions that combine BTC from multiple participants to make tracing individual funds considerably more difficult.

Elliptic Scientist Questions Who Is Operating the Laundering Network

Tom Robinson, Elliptic’s chief scientist and co-founder, highlighted the developing pattern in a Linkedin post Monday, stating:

“At least $247 million (and rising) of the $6.4 billion stolen from Binance has now been passed through coinjoins. Almost all of them coordinated by one individual—Kruw.”

Robinson also drew attention to the increasingly concentrated hours during which the transactions occurred. “This activity is increasingly falling within a core set of daily hours. Certainly not conclusive, but it perhaps suggesting that this crypto has now been passed to China-based launderers, as seen with other NK thefts?”

An accompanying Elliptic chart showed coinjoin activity peaking around 5 a.m. UTC, corresponding to approximately 1 p.m. in China and 2 p.m. in North Korea. The timing offers a possible clue about operational schedules, although it cannot establish where participants are physically located.

Elliptic’s investigation also identified consistent scheduling in the ether movements. Five major addresses were emptied between 6:50 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. UTC, while swaps resumed at precisely 6:50 a.m. UTC on Nov. 23. The researchers characterized the operation as automated, but cautioned against attributing its decisions to artificial intelligence.

Elliptic’s findings note:

“The laundering is clearly automated, but nothing we have seen shows an AI agent making decisions.”

Billions Remain Unmoved as Investigators Follow the Bitcoin

The operation traces back to Binance’s Oct. 29 theft of approximately $6.3 billion across 11 blockchains, which the FBI attributed to North Korea’s Tradertraitor operation. Elliptic estimates that the laundering network has involved more than 27,000 wallets, 16 blockchains, approximately 55 services, and 90,000 transactions.

Despite that extensive activity, approximately $2.22 billion remains in addresses associated with the theft, while another $2.85 billion has been frozen or seized. Notably, the 18,270 BTC stolen directly from Binance has remained untouched since being distributed among 19 addresses immediately after the attack.

The bitcoin entering coinjoins instead originated primarily from other stolen cryptocurrencies converted through cross-chain services. Elliptic’s researchers believe the untouched assets likely remain under North Korean control, while actively laundered funds could have been transferred to outside intermediaries.

“The vast majority of the stolen funds has not yet been cashed out,” the report states.

That distinction remains crucial. Mixing can obscure transaction histories, but converting cryptocurrency into spendable funds generally requires an exchange or broker. For investigators, the latest developments suggest the laundering operation remains active even when its largest conversions pause.

The unresolved question is whether authorities can identify the intermediaries before the stolen assets disappear into increasingly complicated transaction histories. At the time of writing on Monday, Nov. 23, Arkham Intelligence data shows that the hackers still hold close to $1 billion in ether with 522,771.48 ETH stashed in various wallets. Additionally, the thieves hold 29,934.01 WBETH, a liquid staking ETH derivative token issued by Binance.

title: CFTC staff say exchanges can count Bitcoin toward operating reserves
summary: The staff guidance allows Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins to count towards operating reserves.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 23, 2026

The staff guidance allows Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins to count towards operating reserves.

US Commodity Futures Trading Commission staff said Monday that CFTC-regulated derivative exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins toward meeting their financial resource requirements.

CFTC rules require derivatives exchanges, swap trading venues and clearinghouses to maintain enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs on a rolling basis.

The latest staff guidance clarifies that certain crypto assets can count toward part of that requirement, but with a discount to their market value. CFTC staff said they would accept a “haircut” of at least 20% for Bitcoin and Ether and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins to account for the risk of holding those assets.

The guidance gives CFTC-regulated exchanges and entities more flexibility in how they meet their operating reserve requirements. CFTC-regulated entities include Coinbase Derivatives, Crypto.com’s North American Derivatives Exchange and Bitnomial Exchange, as well as prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket US.

However, they will still need to meet a separate liquidity requirement with assets such as cash or highly liquid securities.

The advisory represents the views of staff at the Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk, and is not considered a formal rule change approved by the Commission.

What are OKX Trading Fees?

OKX trading fees are based on the market taker and maker model like many other exchanges. OKX exchange has low trading fees, starting at 0.10% for takers and 0.08% for makers, and higher VIP-level traders will pay lower fees than this standard.

The maker is the trader who created a limit order to sell their crypto. Because this order is not filled immediately, some exchanges, including OKX, charge them lower fees because they add liquidity to the platform. On the flip side, the taker picks up an existing order or purchases the crypto the maker sells from the order book. These traders want their orders filled immediately, thereby taking liquidity away from the platform.

For example, if the current ETH lowest ask price is 2,700 USDT and you create a maker order with a bid price of 2570 USDT, this order cannot be filled immediately. OKX will enter it into the order book until someone (a taker) fills it.

Here is a rundown of the fees for spot, futures, options, and spreads trading on the OKX crypto exchange.

1. Spot Trading Fees

OKX charges regular users 0.10% for takers and 0.08% for makers. The spot interface allows users to buy or sell crypto immediately or when the particular coin reaches a specific price, depending on whether they choose a market or limit order.

Since the platform uses a tiered rating that depends on traders’ 30-day trading volume and the number of OKB tokens the traders hold, transaction fees can be discounted to 0%.

2. Futures Trading Fees

  • Taker Fee: 0.05% for non-VIP users.

The fees are lower for VIP users, with VIP 1 users paying 0.03% (taker) and 0.01% (maker) for futures. The image below summarizes the fees for various VIP levels by trading volume or amount of OKB token the user is holding.

3. Options Trading Fees

OKX Trading Bot

The trading platform offers about 11 bots to help users automate their trades and earn even when they are inactive. The grids include spot and futures grid, futures DCA, smart arbitrage, spot DCA (martingale), recurring buy, signal bot, iceberg, TWAP, smart portfolio, and arbitrage.

Here is a breakdown of how some of these bots help you earn more without constantly monitoring your trades.

  1. Spot Grid

The Spot grid mode splits your starting funds between the two digital assets of your chosen trading pair, say BTC/USDT. The bot then creates a grid of price points between the upper and lower limits and divides your capital equally between the number of grids used.

The bot automatically buys more of the asset when the price drops to a lower grid level. Then, when the price rises to an upper grid level, the spot grid bot automatically sells some of the assets.

Each time the price reaches the upper grid line, the bot automatically sells a portion of the asset and buys the traded asset when the price reaches the lower grid line. You make money from the difference between the prices at which the bot buys and sells.

  1. Futures Grid

The futures grid aims to make money from price fluctuations within a range. OKX offers various types of futures grid strategies:

  • Long Futures Grid: The bot buys futures at the current price and sells them when the price rises. This strategy is best for markets that are expected to go up but still have some volatility.
  • Short Futures Grid: The bot sells futures at the current price and buys them back when the price drops. This strategy is best for markets that expect to go down but still have some volatility.
  • Neutral Futures Grid: The bot trades in both directions, buying when the price is low and selling when it’s high, no matter the market trend.

The goal of the futures grid is to earn small profits from each price movement, whether the market is going up or down or staying within a range.

  1. Smart Arbitrage

OKX smart arbitrage helps traders make steady profits while reducing the risk of price changes in the market. It uses a Delta-neutral strategy, which means holding equal but opposite positions in two markets:

  • Buying a cryptocurrency in the spot market (long position).
  • Selling the same cryptocurrency in the perpetual swap market (short position).

This bot helps balance gains and losses, so price changes have less impact, and profits come from funding fees earned during the holding period. There are two types of smart arbitrage strategies on OKX:

  • Custom Mode: You choose your strategy and set profit targets.
  • Smart Mode: The system recommends the best strategy and automatically manages profit-taking, stop-loss, and adjustments.

Unlike smart arbitrage, there are four ways to set up the OKX futures and spot bots. You can either set the parameters based on your analysis, fill in parameters recommended by the crypto trading bot, use AI strategy, or copy lead traders’ winning bots.

OKX Copy Trading

OKX copy trading is a program that allows new users to copy strategies from more advanced traders and automatically execute them in the spot or futures markets. When you copy a seasoned trader, you will imitate their trades and automatically open and close positions when the trader you copy opens or closes theirs.

Transaction fees for the trades users copy are usually the same as the regular fees for the user’s tier level. However, you will need to share your profit with the lead trader, usually about 8 – 13% of your results. Additionally, you can set a maximum amount per order and a maximum amount for the trader you are copying.

For instance, you can set your maximum amount per order at 50 USDT and your maximum amount for the trader at 500 USDT.  After the lead trader has opened 10 positions, you will have an invested margin of 500 USDT, which is your maximum limit. So, if the trader opens an eleventh position, you won’t copy them.

Remember that the OKX Web3 wallet does not save your seed phrase, private key, or password; you are responsible for these.

OKX Mobile App

OKX offers a mobile app with a user-friendly interface for buying, selling, trading, and managing crypto even when you are on the move. Unlike the desktop interface, the OKX app provides a simple and clean view, perfect for beginners, and an advanced mode for more experienced traders.

In addition, the OKX app offers margin trading with leverage of up to 10X. For derivatives, its futures contracts and perpetual swaps have leverage up to 125X, and you can set alerts to receive notifications when specific changes occur in your trades.

How to Open New Account and Trade on OKX?

If you want to deposit crypto, go to the ‘Assets’ tab and select ‘Deposit.’ Choose the cryptocurrency and the network you want to deposit. Then, transfer the cryptocurrency to the generated wallet address.

Step 2: Choose Your Trading Method

Go to the ‘Trade’ section to see the various trading options OKX crypto exchange offers. Depending on the kind of trade you want to do, choose between spot or derivatives (futures, margin, and perpetual swaps).

For beginners, starting with the spot market or using the copy trading tool to imitate experienced traders is advisable.

Step 3: Place Your First Trade

Select the pair you want from the spot or futures market, like PEPE/USDT or BTC/USDT. Since this is your first trade, we recommend you use a small amount of money to trade.

Use the order window on the right to place buy or sell orders. You can choose between different order types:

  • Market Orders: Execute immediately at current prices.
  • Limit Orders: Set a specific price you want to buy or sell crypto.
  • Stop Orders: Execute when a certain price condition is met.

Finally, confirm your order, and it will be executed according to the order types you choose.

Does OKX Require KYC?

Yes, OKX does require KYC. The process is similar to that of other exchanges. To confirm your identity, you must submit personal identification documents, such as a selfie, a passport, or a driver’s license. Ensure that the information on your ID matches the region/country you picked during the account registration process.

Is OKX Safe and Legit to Trade Crypto and Bitcoin?

OKX is safe and legitimate to trade crypto and Bitcoin. The platform is considered as one of the best cryptocurrency exchanges with the cleanest interfaces. It is designed with simple and advanced modes to cater to various users. Additionally, if you are a beginner, the mobile app is better for learning, and you don’t have to worry about missing anything because it has all the features on the desktop version.

OKX offers some security features, including offline asset storage, a risk shield, multi-factor authentication, passkeys, anti-phishing codes, and withdrawal address whitelisting.

  1. Cold Wallet Storage

95% of assets on OKX are stored in offline wallets, which are not susceptible to hacks and security breaches. The company limits how much cryptocurrency can be stored in a single cold wallet address to further protect user funds assets stored offline.

Each address can hold a maximum of 1,000 BTC. This spreads the total amount of offline assets across multiple wallets, preventing a single point of failure. Once the funds in one cold wallet are withdrawn, new deposits will no longer be received.

  1. OKX Risk Shield

OKX crypto exchange sets aside a percentage of the platform’s assets, over $700 million, to safeguard money and users from potential breaches. The risk fund is similar to Binance’s Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), which protects against security breaches and market volatility.

3. Multi-factor Authentication

Once you open an account on OKX, it is important to up your security. You can do this through the profile icon. There, you will find various security measures to activate.

Start with two-factor authentication (2FA), then activate passkeys and authenticators. If you decide to activate the Google Authenticator app, keep the code you will be given safely. If you lose your phone or change devices, you can use it to log in to your authenticator app.

4. Anti-phishing Codes

This security feature allows users to double-proof their account security. When you activate it, OKX will email you a code that helps you differentiate between legitimate communications and suspicious emails.

5. Proof of Reserves

OKX published their December 2024 proof of reserve data and they’re holding over USD 30.8 billion in reserves. This includes some of the most popular cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin (105%), Ethereum (102%), and stablecoins such as Tether USDT (106%) and USD Coin (100%).

The PoR is published monthly, and the company uses advanced cryptographic methods, including zero-knowledge proofs, to ensure full transparency while protecting user privacy. You can independently verify your assets through OKX’s dashboard and public wallet addresses.

6. Withdrawal Address Whitelisting

OKX allows users to choose which wallet addresses are allowed for withdrawals through the address whitelisting feature. Any address outside the pre-approved addresses will automatically be blocked. So, even if someone tries to hack into your account, they cannot move funds to any address since they are not on the list.

content:
2026-11-23T23:12:54.924+02:00

Monday, 23/11/2026 | 21:12 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Kraken refused to cancel trades after a local flash crash sent its BTC/CAD pair plunging to C$24,250 (~$17,000).
  • The hands-off stance contrasts sharply with the 2015 Swiss franc shock, when principal dealer Saxo UK retroactively rewrote confirmed client fills.

Kraken let deeply discounted BTC/CAD trades stand, leaving buyers and sellers with the prices at which their orders matched. After the 2015 Swiss franc shock, Saxo Capital Markets UK made a different choice: it changed prices already confirmed to clients.

The disputes that followed show why the time of execution and the liquidity available then matter when a firm decides whether a fill should stand.IKraken Leaves Discounted BTC/CAD Fills Intact

On 21 November Bitcoin changed hands for as low as C$24,250 (around US$17,000) on the Kraken BTC/CAD market whilst the BTC/USD price was hovering at $57,700.

CoinDesk counted some 245 BTC traded over 15 minute intervals in which the average price of the CAD pair was below C$50,000. A separate look at Kraken's trade data revealed 122 trades involving 10.69 BTC below the equivalent of US$20,000 in the quarter hour around the low.

Kraken attributed the move to heavy selling in its CAD pairs, said it found no breach or compromised accounts, and confirmed that the trades would stand, meaning the buyers in those trades keep the Bitcoin they acquired; sellers keep the Canadian dollars they received.

Kraken's trading rules state that completed trades are final and binding, but allow for protection against wide spreads. According to the Canadian regulator, the company has policies to cancel, vary or correct trades, but Kraken has elected to leave the trades in place.

Starting around 20:00 UTC on Nov 20, CAD pairs on Kraken saw heavy selling pressure that pushed prices well below other markets. Our platform processed every order correctly, and our security teams found no sign of a breach or compromised accounts. Executed trades stand.

— Kraken Support (@krakensupport) November 21, 2026

Saxo Changed Confirmed Prices and Regretted It

Saxo took the other course after the 2015 Swiss franc shock: it revised prices already confirmed to clients, who then challenged the decision.

Because Saxo had traded with those clients as principal, the UK Financial Ombudsman Service examined the broker’s terms alongside the prices and liquidity available when each position closed.

One client's EUR/CHF options were closed at 09:30 a.m., shortly after the Swiss National Bank’s announcement. Saxo subsequently changed the price and the client's account was left with a significant liability.

The UK Financial Ombudsman Service ordered Saxo to reverse the price adjustment. They found the price was within the market and there was sufficient liquidity at the time of the trade closing. They also found no basis in the client's terms for Saxo Bank to pass on any losses arising from its own hedging.

Another client's EUR/CHF CFD trades closed at 9.34 am the same day. But the market conditions had already changed significantly. In that complaint the ombudsman accepted Saxo's new price as being the correct one as it was based on the EBS trades at that time.

The same market shock had produced different results for trades which had been executed minutes apart.

Ultimately, the contrast between Saxo’s 2015 repricing and Kraken’s hands-off stance comes down to who bears the cost of an empty order book. Saxo learned the hard way that a broker cannot retroactively rewrite confirmed fills simply because its own hedging failed minutes later.

Kraken took the opposite path: even though its regulatory rulebook allows the exchange to keep or adjust trades executed across abnormally wide spreads, it chose to treat the C$24,250 flash crash as legitimate price discovery inside an isolated currency pair.

Until exchanges enforce automated circuit breakers linking regional fiat books to USD liquidity, traders dumping large market orders into regional pairs remain one thin bid away from an irreversible haircut.

title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
Strive bought no bitcoin and sold no stock last week, leaving holdings at 43,404 BTC, its Monday 8-K shows. ASST shares traded near $15.55.
This post Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,40...
content:
Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing.

The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close.

Strive pauses after two small buys

The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that.

Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion.

The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again.

Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run.

Cash and preferred holdings

Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change.

The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged.

Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases.

Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations.

Shares rally, then fade with the market

Strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session.

The swing tracked bitcoin-linked stocks broadly after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang and sent equities sharply higher, a move Bitcoin Magazine covered earlier Monday. Bitcoin spiked above $64,000 in the morning before sliding back toward $61,000 during U.S. trading hours.

The stock has lost much of its October run. ASST closed at $30.75 on Oct. 21, so Monday’s price is about 49% lower. It is still roughly 5% above its 2025 year-end close of $14.76.

Strive’s preferred stocks remain a central part of its model. On Nov. 12, the board raised the SATA dividend rate to 13.25% for periods beginning Dec. 1, while SATS continues to pay 15%. Both pay daily cash dividends, so the company’s cash balance funds a steady outflow even in weeks without purchases.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,000.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: US seeks to recover $1.1B in crypto stolen in North Korea-linked Binance hack
summary: US prosecutors are seeking control of stolen USDC, while Elliptic says hackers have moved $247 million through Bitcoin mixers.
content:
The US Department of Justice is seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in crypto stolen from cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October by hackers linked to North Korea.

In a court filing Monday, prosecutors asked a federal court in Washington, DC, to permanently forfeit the funds, which are held in USDC – a stablecoin issued by Circle. The filing follows a court order obtained earlier this month allowing authorities to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in assets linked to the hack. Since the attack, which occurred on Oct. 29, US authorities said they have helped to freeze, seize or return nearly $3 billion of the more than $6 billion taken from Binance.

“Following the Binance theft, the FBI and our partners moved quickly to trace and freeze stolen assets and share critical information with virtual asset service providers,” said in a statement Brett Leatherman, operations director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) cyber branch.

Binance has also pursued legal action to recover the stolen assets. On Nov. 18, the exchange said it had secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts. The orders target unidentified attackers and allow legal notices to be delivered through blockchain transactions to wallets linked to the theft.

Hackers move stolen funds across thousands of wallets

The filing comes as blockchain analytics firm Elliptic also reported an analysis updated Monday that hackers had moved at least $247 million in Bitcoin (BTC) through crypto mixers – tools that make stolen funds harder to track. The firm said another $2.22 billion remained in wallets linked to the theft, while $2.85 billion had been frozen or seized.

Elliptic noted that hackers had moved stolen funds through more than 27,000 wallets across at least 16 blockchains. However, most of the crypto had not yet been converted into cash, and the 18,270 BTC stolen directly from Binance had not moved since the attack.

US authorities have linked the attack to a North Korean hacking group called TraderTraitor. According to Binance, the hackers gained access to its systems after tricking an employee into downloading malicious software. Following the attack, Binance said it had committed more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses and reassured that customer funds were safe.

Related: As it happened: Binance’s record $6.3B crypto hack

title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
The bitcoin price gave back its Nvidia-fueled spike above $64,000 on Monday afternoon, slipping near $61,000 while stocks and crypto shares held big gains.
This post Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on...
content:
The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours, and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day.

The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million, with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million.

Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades

Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday.

Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned.

A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40, its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case.

Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said.

Crypto stocks keep most of their gains

Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33.

Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%.

ETF flows and inflation data are next

Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100.

“Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. Strong inflows would suggest buyers are returning, while another round of outflows would raise doubts about how far the rebound can run.

Traders also face Wednesday’s inflation data and thin trading around Thanksgiving in a holiday-shortened week. Wintermute OTC trader Jasper De Maere said he isn’t ready to call a bottom for the bitcoin price. “A few days of data do not confirm a trend and these series turn slowly,” he said.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,100.

Micah Zimmerman

title: Kalshi secures temporary win in New York gambling law dispute
summary: The ruling allows Kalshi to continue operating as its legal battle with New York over sports-related event contracts moves toward a January hearing.
content:
A New York state court judge on Monday denied the state attorney general’s request for a temporary restraining order against prediction market operator Kalshi, allowing the company to continue offering event contracts in New York as a legal battle over its sports-related markets proceeds.

In a statement to Cointelegraph, Elisabeth Diana, Kalshi’s head of communications, confirmed the ruling, saying the judge recognized the complex legal questions surrounding derivatives and federal preemption.

“The judge denied the State’s request for a TRO, recognizing that there are complex questions about derivatives and preemption. We remain committed to working with the State on a path forward that works for our 1.5 million customers and for the state of New York,” Diana said.

Source: Trace Schmeltz

The denial of the temporary restraining order does not resolve the broader dispute over whether Kalshi’s federally regulated event contracts are subject to New York’s gambling laws.

The case will now proceed toward a preliminary injunction hearing set for early January, when the court will consider whether to restrict Kalshi’s event-contract operations in New York. Before then, both parties are scheduled to return to court on Nov. 30 to discuss potential restrictions on users aged 18 to 20, following concerns raised by the judge over the state’s minimum legal age of 21 for sports betting.

Related: CFTC halts some Kalshi Trump mention markets over manipulation concerns

Kalshi challenges state gambling regulations

New York sued Kalshi in July, alleging the prediction market operator was running an illegal, unlicensed gambling business by offering event contracts tied to sports, elections and other outcomes. The lawsuit seeks to halt the company’s operations in the state, recover alleged illegal gains and impose civil penalties.

The case followed an October 2025 cease-and-desist order from the New York State Gaming Commission, which prompted Kalshi to challenge the state’s authority in federal court. Kalshi argues that its status as a federally regulated derivatives exchange places its event contracts under the jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

In August, the CFTC warned that New York’s requested restraining order could prevent Kalshi from offering event contracts nationwide because the exchange is based in the state. The regulator also said New York was seeking more than $36 billion in damages.

In a separate federal court proceeding on Friday, US District Judge Lorna Schofield rejected the CFTC’s emergency request to block New York from pursuing its enforcement case against Kalshi, according to Reuters.

Kalshi isn’t the only prediction market operator facing legal action in New York. The state also sued Polymarket in September over allegedly offering illegal sports betting contracts, following similar actions against platforms operated by Coinbase and Gemini in April.

title: BTCS offloads $44M in ETH to reduce DeFi debt amid market downturn
summary: BTCS sold more than half its Ether holdings to reduce leverage following the market sell-off, while BitMine added another 7,819 ETH to its treasury.
content:
Nasdaq-listed blockchain company BTCS sold approximately 27,300 Ether on Friday to repay $43.8 million in loans on decentralized lending protocol Aave as cryptocurrency markets plunged.

According to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, BTCS sold the Ether (ETH) on Nov. 20 and used the proceeds to reduce its outstanding Aave debt to approximately $10.5 million.

The transaction reduced BTCS’s Aave borrowings by approximately 81%, as the company sought to limit liquidation risk amid heightened market volatility. Its remaining Aave positions had a loan-to-value ratio of approximately 32% following the repayment.

BTCS reported approximately $17.9 million in outstanding convertible notes, in addition to its remaining Aave borrowings, according to the company’s announcement. The company also said it temporarily exited liquidity pool positions in its Imperium DeFi business as part of its efforts to reduce exposure to further market volatility.

Following the sale, BTCS held approximately 24,245 ETH, with cash and digital assets valued at a combined $61 million as of Sunday. The 27,300 ETH sale represented approximately 53% of its combined pre-sale ETH holdings.

The move follows a similar reduction in Ether exposure by digital asset manager CoinShares, which disclosed last week that it sold its entire ETH treasury position and half its Solana (SOL) holdings in October to fund share buybacks.

Related: Bitmine edges toward 5% of ETH supply as treasuries report buys amid market slump

BitMine continues Ether accumulation

Meanwhile, Tom Lee’s BitMine Immersion Technologies continued accumulating Ether, purchasing another 7,819 ETH over the past week despite the market downturn.

According to a Monday announcement, BitMine now holds 6,085,564 ETH, representing 4.98% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply. The company said it has purchased Ether every week since adopting its treasury strategy in June 2025.

BitMine also reported $384 million in cash and marketable securities as of Sunday. The company has staked approximately 5.23 million ETH, representing 86% of its total Ether holdings.

BitMine accounts for roughly 75% of the Ether held in corporate and government treasuries tracked by CoinGecko, which listed 35 entities holding a combined 8.16 million ETH at the time of reporting.

The contrasting strategies come as Ether continues to struggle, trading at approximately $1,743 as of 6:35 p.m. UTC on Monday, down 37.7% over the past year and 24.8% over the past 30 days, according to CoinGecko data.

2026-11-23T20:35:56.014+02:00

Monday, 23/11/2026 | 18:35 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Global brokerage, liquidity, and fintech executives gathered at The Folly in the City of London for the Opening Networking Blitz kicking off the 15th edition of Finance Magnates Summit London.
  • The summit moves to Old Billingsgate on Tuesday, headlined by CMC Markets founder Lord Peter Cruddas on tokenisation and a live audience-voted debate on retail access to prediction markets.

The Finance Magnates Summit in London got off to the traditional start on Monday evening with the Opening Networking Blitz. The party brought together brokers, liquidity providers, and fintech people to network ahead of the conference and exhibition on Tuesday.

TheBlitz is back at The Folly, a bar and restaurant on Gracechurch Street in the City, with greenery hanging over the bar and a garden-style lounge. Over drinks and a bite to eat, guests could catch up with familiar faces and meet new contacts through introductions arranged by the organisers.

Guests can also meet the Money Ready team, a UK financial education charity, and support its work.

A One-Day Summit at Old Billingsgate

The summit returns to Old Billingsgate for its 15th edition on Tuesday 24th November. This year the conference and exhibition will run on the same day, creating opportunities for one-to-one meetings for exhibitors and sponsors and running a number of invitation-only roundtables, including one on what crypto product brokers could be offering in 2027.

CMC Markets founder and CEO Lord Peter Cruddas will discuss how retail trading has changed since he set up the brokerage and what tokenisation could mean for the industry.

A separate panel will examine what financial firms need to use stablecoins for settlement, from choosing issuers to safeguarding assets. The Vision Stage will close with a debate on whether retail investors should be barred from prediction markets.

Gerald Perez of Interactive Brokers UK will argue against a ban, and Laura McCracken of Blackheath Advisors will make the case for one. The audience will vote on the motion.

The Evening Gets Under Way at The Folly

Here’s a first look inside The Folly. We’ll add photos and updates from the room as the evening unfolds.

In the kitchen, plates of small bites are lined up under the heat lamps, ready to go out to guests.

The bar is filling up. Guests stand shoulder to shoulder along the counter, catching up over drinks.

The Blitz in Full Swing

Away from the bar, a group has pulled up stools around a high table.

Behind the counter, The Folly’s bartenders are mixing drinks beneath the Christmas garlands while conversations carry on across the bar.

By the lounge, summit lanyards and badge holders hang from a stand. Delegates can pick up their badges at the Blitz ahead of Tuesday’s programme at Old Billingsgate.

title: Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
Bitdeer mined 281.1 BTC last week and sold all of it, leaving the miner with no bitcoin of its own as of Nov. 20 while American Bitcoin borrows against its reserve instead.
This post Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined...
content:
Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price.

The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20.

The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday.

Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year

Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market.

Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier.

Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025.

Self-mining margins stay thin

Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows.

The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash.

Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party.

Bitdeer also reported $213.7 million in cash and restricted cash, and its board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program on Oct. 8.

Borrowing against coins instead of selling them

Not every miner is selling. American Bitcoin secured a $150 million revolving credit line from FalconX on Monday that is backed by its bitcoin. The company said the facility lets it raise cash without drawing down its reserve.

The loan carries a 5.95% fee and an initial collateral ratio of 143%. Fully drawing it would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin. American Bitcoin has not said whether it has drawn on the line, and its release lists the risk that pledged coins could be liquidated if prices fall.

American Bitcoin, which is majority-owned by Hut 8, said on its Nov. 4 earnings call that it held 8,427 BTC at the end of September. The company has also sold part of its production to cover operating costs.

Other miners have gone the other way. MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin earlier this month, as miners facing thin margins turned to their treasuries for cash.

BTDR rallies with the market

Shares of Bitdeer (BTDR) were trading near $3.44 at 11:23 AM ET, up about 16% from Friday’s close of $2.96. The stock has ranged from $3.26 to $3.71 on the day as a broad market rally lifted bitcoin-linked stocks after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang.

Bitdeer has not said whether it plans to rebuild a bitcoin position. It said in February that selling was a liquidity measure tied to evaluating powered land acquisitions and scaling its infrastructure.

The company is also shifting toward AI cloud services, and it reported an AI cloud revenue backlog of about $2.9 billion in its third-quarter release.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $62,700.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board’s Unanimous Vote
summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and chief executive officer following a unanimous board vote, reversing his sudden departure less than two weeks ago.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVDA

Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and chief executive officer following a unanimous board vote, reversing his sudden departure less than two weeks ago.

The decision returns the company’s co-founder to its top leadership position amid ongoing investigations and heightened scrutiny over national security concerns.

In a November 23 announcement, Nvidia confirmed that Huang had also resumed his position as a member of the board, effective immediately. The decision followed several discussions and meetings between Huang and directors, who said they were satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company.

The board also considered input from senior U.S. government officials before approving his return. According to Nvidia, that input gave directors confidence that reinstating Huang would not create a national security risk.

Nvidia Board Unanimously Approves Jensen Huang’s Return

Harvey C. Jones, Nvidia’s board chair, said directors believe Huang remains the right person to lead the company through its next phase of growth.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Jones said in the announcement.

NVIDIA’s board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director effective immediately, reversing a recent CEO transition. Source: @nvidianewsroom/X

The decision marks a significant reversal from the leadership changes announced earlier in November. On November 12, Nvidia disclosed that Huang had resigned as president, CEO, and board director, effective immediately. The board subsequently appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning the process of identifying a permanent successor.

Huang’s departure followed reports involving personal relationships and concerns about a possible foreign intelligence operation. Media coverage also raised questions about potential national security implications involving individuals connected to China.

According to subsequent reporting by Reuters and The Associated Press, the circumstances surrounding his departure attracted attention from U.S. authorities and prompted broader scrutiny of the company’s leadership and compliance arrangements.

Huang’s reinstatement does not bring the internal investigation to an end. Nvidia confirmed that the independent committee established to examine reports of a foreign intelligence effort targeting its founder will continue its work until completion.

Foreign Intelligence Investigation Remains Open

Nvidia initially announced its independent investigation on November 8, following reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

The company appointed a committee consisting exclusively of independent directors and retained outside legal counsel to oversee the inquiry. The board said at the time that it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia’s confidential information had been compromised, although it intended to examine all available information.

The November 23 announcement maintains that commitment. Nvidia said Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate fully until the process concludes.

The distinction is important: the board’s assessment that his return presents no national security risk does not mean the underlying investigation has been completed.

The company’s latest decision also follows public support for Huang’s return from prominent figures, including U.S. President Donald Trump. Brave New Coin reported that Trump had encouraged Nvidia to bring its founder back after the board initially indicated that reinstatement was not under consideration.

The president subsequently welcomed the reversal, describing it as the correct decision.

Nevertheless, questions surrounding the circumstances of Huang’s departure remain relevant to the company’s governance and regulatory responsibilities. Nvidia has also faced scrutiny over potential export-control and other compliance issues, according to media reports.

Nvidia Establishes New Compliance Oversight

Alongside Huang’s reinstatement, Nvidia is introducing additional governance measures intended to strengthen oversight of national security risks and international trade compliance.

The board has established a National Security and Export Control Committee, consisting entirely of independent directors. Its responsibilities include supervising trade compliance and assessing national security risks associated with the company’s operations.

NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has formed a dedicated committee to oversee national security and export control matters. Source: @nvidianewsroom/X

The committee is also engaging legal counsel with experience in national security matters. Those advisers will bring in additional specialists to support its work.

Nvidia is separately beginning a search for a Chief Compliance Officer. The new executive will oversee compliance across the company and report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.

These measures indicate that Nvidia intends to maintain closer oversight of regulatory and security-related matters even as Huang returns to executive leadership.

Jones also acknowledged Kress’s contribution during the transition, thanking her for managing the company as interim CEO while continuing her responsibilities as chief financial officer.

Kress will now return to her previous executive responsibilities. She has served as the company’s CFO since September 2013 and has been responsible for overseeing its financial organization during a period of substantial expansion.

Jensen Huang Signals Renewed Commitment to Nvidia

In his statement following the reinstatement, Huang expressed appreciation for the board’s decision and acknowledged the responsibility of returning to lead the company.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said.

He also thanked Jones, Kress, Nvidia’s executive team, employees, shareholders, and business partners for their support during the leadership transition.

Jensen Huang updates his X bio and adds “CEO of Nvidia” to his title. Source: @JensenHuang/X

Huang described Nvidia as one of the world’s most consequential technology companies and said he was eager to resume his responsibilities.

His return restores the company’s familiar leadership structure at a time when demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to shape the semiconductor industry.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has overseen its transformation from a graphics processing unit manufacturer into a central supplier of computing hardware and software for artificial intelligence, data centers, and accelerated computing.

That history has made his leadership closely associated with the company’s corporate strategy and long-term direction. His unexpected departure therefore created uncertainty around the company’s succession planning and executive decision-making.

Nvidia Stock Rallies Following Leadership Reversal

Financial markets reacted positively to the reinstatement announcement. According to Reuters, Nvidia shares surged approximately 33% in early trading on November 23, as investors responded to the return of its long-serving founder.

The announcement also helped revive sentiment across technology and artificial intelligence stocks following recent weakness in the sector. Reuters reported gains in broader U.S. equity benchmarks, including the Nasdaq and S&P 500, during the session.

However, the immediate market reaction does not resolve the governance and regulatory questions surrounding Nvidia. Investors will continue monitoring the independent investigation, the company’s compliance initiatives, and any further developments involving U.S. authorities.

For now, Huang’s return restores continuity at the top of Nvidia while placing additional responsibility on its board to demonstrate that the company can maintain effective oversight.

The independent investigation will continue, and Nvidia has pledged to cooperate with government inquiries. The outcome of those processes, alongside the implementation of its new compliance framework, will remain important developments for the company in the coming weeks.
