title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
A solo miner with about 11.1 TH/s found Bitcoin block 977,057 through CKpool, collecting 3.1287 BTC. The CKpool developer put the odds at about 1 in 1,650 a year.
This post Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward...
content:
A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network.

The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed.

How the solo block played out

The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000.

Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.”

He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote.

The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node.

A recent run of solo wins

Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page. The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC.

Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC.

Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee.

Network hashrate and difficulty

Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining.

Mining difficulty is about 134.8 trillion. The last adjustment cut it by about 9.1%, and the next one, expected around Nov. 26, is estimated to raise it by about 9.2%, according to mempool.space. Difficulty resets every 2,016 blocks to keep blocks arriving about every 10 minutes.

Mining conditions have been tough. Bitcoin plunged to about $55,100 over the weekend before rebounding to near $64,000 on Monday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro. Lower prices cut the dollar value of every block, whether it goes to an industrial miner or a hobbyist running a small solo rig.

The subsidy is fixed at 3.125 BTC until the next halving, so what the solo winner earns depends on fees and the market. A 3.1287 BTC block was worth about $196,000 at Monday’s price near $62,700, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $62,700.

Micah Zimmerman

summary:

On November 23, 2026, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Hong Kong issued a restriction ...
content:
2026-11-23T19:18:11.337+02:00

Monday, 23/11/2026 | 17:18 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Regulators suspect the firm raided client balances to meet margin calls and cover trading losses generated by other accounts.
  • SFC says the restrictions are needed to protect the interests of the broker's clients.

The regulator has limited the operations of the Hong Kong-based futures broker DA YUE Financial Group after the authorities uncovered an alleged $29.6 million hole in its segregated client accounts.

On November 23, 2026, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Hong Kong issued a restriction notice for DA YUE Financial Group Limited (DYFGL).

The regulator said the measures are needed "to preserve the assets of DYFGL’s clients, and to protect the interests of these clients and the investing public".

Raiding Segregated Accounts to Cover Margin Calls

DA YUE is a Hong Kong-based broker providing access to global futures trading venues including HKEX, CME and LME. In April 2021, the company received an SFC licence to deal in and advise on futures contracts.

According to the regulatory data, the company has 270 active clients with positive account balances. It was supposed to keep customers' assets segregated on separate trust accounts in authorised banks, yowever, the SFC's initial enquiries revealed that DYFGL had a client money shortfall of about $29.6 million.

The regulator believes that the broker "used client money to meet the margin requirements and cover the futures trading losses of certain other clients", violating the licence requirements.

To stop the breach and protect the clients' money, the SFC issued a restriction notice prohibiting the company from carrying out any of the regulated activities without the SFC’s prior written consent and disposing of any assets, including those held on behalf of its clients.

"This raises concerns about DYFGL’s reliability, integrity and ability to carry on its regulated activities competently, honestly and fairly, and calls into question whether it remains fit and proper to be licensed," the regulator said in the restriction notice.

At the same time, DYFGL is still allowed to deposit money in its own accounts with an authorised financial institution and pay its operational expenses.

Brokerage Shutdown vs. Targeted Account Freezes

The SFC presents the restrictions as preventive measures, while it continues investigating the potential violations. The regulator often uses this measure against customers' accounts suspected of wrongdoing.

Thus in 2026, the Commission issued a restriction notice to Futu Securities International (Hong Kong) Limited. The notice bars Futu from dealing with or processing up to HK$125,247,000 in client accounts held by an entity suspected of a fraudulent scheme to create a false appearance of demand in an IPO.

However, unlike DYFGL, Futu is not the subject of the investigation, and the notice does not affect Futu or its other clients. For the broker’s 270 active clients, the freeze leaves account balances in limbo until the SFC completes its investigation of the $29.6 million gap.

Should it confirm intentional misappropriation of trust funds, DA YUE faces permanent licence revocation, potential criminal referrals, and the appointment of administrators to unwind its remaining positions.

title: Meta AI Chief Alexandr Wang: Superintelligence Is Coming, Human Control at Risk
summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang has warned that artificial superintelligence could soon surpass human capabilities across nearly every field, raising urgent questions about AI safety, alignment, and humanity’s ability to retain control.
content:
Skip to content

Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang has warned that artificial superintelligence could soon surpass human capabilities across nearly every field, raising urgent questions about AI safety, alignment, and humanity’s ability to retain control.

In an essay published on X on November 22, Wang argued that recent developments in AI-assisted mathematics signal a significant shift in technological progress. He said decisions made over the next year could help determine how society manages increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems.

Riemann Hypothesis Breakthrough Raises Superintelligence Concerns

Wang pointed to a claimed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, developed by mathematician Levent Alpöge with assistance from Anthropic’s Claude, as evidence of how rapidly AI capabilities are advancing.

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang called an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis evidence of superintelligence, surpassing the atomic bomb in intellectual difficulty. Source: Alexandr Wang via X

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and remains one of mathematics’ most challenging unsolved problems. It is also among the seven Millennium Prize Problems established by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for an accepted solution to each problem.

Alpöge released approximately 17 million lines of code written in Lean, a formal proof assistant that allows mathematical arguments to be checked computationally. The Lean and Mathlib communities subsequently expressed confidence in the formal verification, marking an important development in AI-assisted mathematical research.

However, the result has not yet received formal acceptance from the Clay Mathematics Institute. Questions have also emerged about the formalization, while mathematicians continue to examine whether the underlying argument can be understood and validated independently.

Wang viewed the development as evidence that AI systems are approaching a new level of intellectual capability. Describing the achievement, he referred to the assistance of an “alien mind that we don’t understand.”

He also compared the mathematical challenge with historical scientific achievements, writing that many physicists would consider the discovery of the atomic bomb “a homework problem compared to the Riemann Hypothesis.”

For Wang, the significance extends beyond mathematics. He believes that AI systems are approaching a level of reasoning that could allow them to outperform highly skilled humans in increasingly complex intellectual tasks.

AI Intelligence Is No Longer the Main Bottleneck

Wang argued that the limitations preventing AI from surpassing human performance are shifting away from raw intelligence toward practical challenges. These include specialized knowledge, technical integration, experimentation, and access to reliable feedback.

He recalled the progress made by OpenAI’s o3 reasoning model in the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) in December 2024. According to Wang, the model’s performance on difficult mathematical problems demonstrated that AI systems already possessed substantial reasoning capabilities.

Alexandr Wang declared that superintelligence is emerging, citing an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as evidence of machines surpassing human intellectual capabilities. Source: @JOBhakdi/X

The remaining challenge, he explained, was applying those capabilities to specialized fields that require contextual understanding, technical expertise, and real-world experimentation.

Wang said the AI industry has made considerable progress in addressing these limitations over the past two years. He pointed to advances in software development, cybersecurity, and agentic capabilities that allow AI systems to perform increasingly complex tasks with less direct human involvement.

He argued that similar progress could extend across scientific research, business, and other professional disciplines.

“The remaining gaps for models to greatly surpass humanity in every field are no longer intelligence; they are domain-specific know-how, plumbing, and experimentation,” Wang wrote.

His assessment suggests that improvements in how AI systems access information, interact with external tools, and conduct experiments could become increasingly important to future capability gains.

Recursive Self-Improvement Raises Human Control Risks

One of Wang’s central concerns involves the possibility that advanced AI systems could eventually automate significant parts of AI research itself.

He argued that models may become capable of improving their own development processes, potentially accelerating technological progress beyond the pace at which human researchers can understand or monitor it.

Wang warned of risks from uncontrolled recursive self-improvement and vastly smarter AI, while stressing that such an outcome is not inevitable. Source: Alexandr Wang via X

Such developments could also affect fields beyond computer science. Wang identified biological research, weapons research, and economics as areas that could experience substantial acceleration as AI systems become more capable.

The concern is particularly relevant to recursive self-improvement, a process in which AI systems contribute to developing more capable versions of themselves. If that process becomes increasingly autonomous, technological progress could outpace existing oversight mechanisms.

Wang questioned whether humanity could maintain meaningful control over systems operating at a level far beyond human intelligence.

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” he wrote.

He also raised concerns about the possibility of superintelligent systems becoming 1,000 times more capable than humans across different fields.

However, these statements represent Wang’s assessment of the direction of AI development rather than confirmation that unrestricted self-improvement or artificial superintelligence has already been achieved.

Meta AI Chief Calls for Urgent Safety and Alignment Measures

Wang argued that AI safety, alignment, and security must receive greater attention as developers build increasingly capable models.

AI alignment involves ensuring that artificial intelligence systems behave consistently with human intentions, values, and established safety requirements. Researchers are also working to improve model interpretability and monitoring so developers can better understand how advanced systems make decisions.

Wang criticized what he described as a tendency within the AI industry to treat artificial superintelligence (ASI) as inevitable while viewing safety as the only remaining challenge.

He argued that society should not accept an automatic transfer of decision-making power to increasingly capable machines.

“We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI,” Wang wrote.

Instead, he called for a different approach to AI development that prioritizes human agency and empowerment. He said the industry should move away from its current development trajectory to ensure technological progress produces positive outcomes for society.

His comments are particularly notable because Wang leads Meta Superintelligence Labs, the company’s division focused on developing advanced AI systems. However, his essay presented his personal assessment and did not announce a new Meta safety policy or development restriction.

OpenAI and US Lawmakers Raise Broader AI Safety Concerns

Wang’s warning comes amid growing discussions about whether the AI industry needs shared restrictions and stronger oversight as model capabilities advance.

OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed industry-wide limits on AI development in a November 22 essay. He argued that developers should establish common benchmarks for measuring model capabilities and agree not to exceed certain thresholds until monitoring and safety systems improve.

Pachocki suggested using perplexity, a technical measurement of how effectively a model predicts the next piece of text, alongside other indicators to compare progress across AI developers.

“I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone,” he wrote.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman supported the proposal, describing Pachocki’s essay as one of the company’s most important recent publications. The proposal reflects growing interest in establishing shared standards rather than allowing individual companies to determine development limits independently.

US Senator Bernie Sanders has also pushed for stronger restrictions. In September 2026, Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which seeks to prohibit the development and deployment of superintelligent AI and temporarily pause advanced AI development until federal safety rules are established.

The proposed legislation also calls for a dedicated federal agency to oversee advanced AI systems and pursue international agreements to prevent the development of superintelligence.

These initiatives highlight a broader debate over how governments, technology companies, and researchers should manage the risks associated with increasingly powerful AI systems.

The Next Year Could Shape the Future of AI Development

Wang concluded that decisions made over the next year could have significant consequences for the future relationship between humans and artificial intelligence.

His warning reflects growing disagreement within the technology industry over whether rapid AI development should continue under existing frameworks or be accompanied by coordinated safety requirements and stronger oversight.

The Riemann Hypothesis development has added another dimension to that debate, although questions surrounding its formalization and mathematical interpretation remain unresolved.

For now, Wang’s central argument is that AI progress should not be measured solely by how quickly systems become more capable. Developers must also consider whether humans can understand, supervise, and meaningfully direct the technology they create.

As companies compete to build increasingly advanced models, the challenge will be balancing technological progress with safeguards that preserve human oversight and decision-making.

summary:
Nvidia has reinstated
Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, effective immediately today (Monday),
following calls from US President Donald Trump for his return. Huang resigned
on November 12.
London's trading industry is coming home!
Nvidia shares surged

content:
2026-11-23T17:36:24.868+02:00

Monday, 23/11/2026 | 15:36 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Trump backs Huang's return, calling the board's decision the "correct and proper decision."
  • SEC and DOJ investigations into Nvidia continue despite Huang's return.

Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, effective immediately today (Monday), following calls from US President Donald Trump for his return. Huang resigned on November 12.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Nvidia shares surged 33% following the announcement, reversing the market reaction to his departure less than two weeks ago.

Trump Backs Huang as Nvidia CEO Again

Huang stepped down following reports of several alleged extramarital relationships, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for China. Beijing denies the allegation. Huang was also alleged to have had relationships with at least two Nvidia employees.

Last week, Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said the board would not rehire Huang despite growing calls for his return. Trump subsequently urged the company to reconsider, describing Monday's reinstatement as the "correct and proper decision."

Nvidia said its board voted unanimously to restore Huang after reviewing his conduct and leadership. The directors said they were satisfied with his candor and leadership ability. After consulting senior US government officials, they concluded that his return posed no national security risk.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director. Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil

— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 23, 2026

Nvidia Faces Scrutiny Over Accounting and “Chip Smuggling”

Trump said the US government had no evidence that Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. However, he urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls.

The leadership change comes as Nvidia faces multiple investigations, including inquiries by the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Justice. These cover potential accounting issues and alleged “chip smuggling”.

The board has also formed a committee to examine whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang. Nvidia is separately searching for a new chief compliance officer. Colette Kress will remain chief financial officer.

Armitage and Superform build a stock-strategy franchise on SuperformOS
summary: New York City, USA, 23rd November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

New York City, USA, 23rd November 2026, Chainwire

New York City, USA, November 23rd, 2026, Chainwire

Eight existing SuperStocks strategies move under Armitage’s curation, with SuperformOS providing the operating system behind the products.

Armitage, Wintermute’s onchain vault curation arm, and Superform today announced a collaboration that gives holders of tokenized NVIDIA, Tesla, Apple and five other stocks an option beyond holding or selling. Armitage will curate Superform’s Earn Stocks strategies on Base. Built on SuperformOS, these strategies let holders use their tokenized stocks as collateral while keeping their stock exposure.

Holders deposit their tokenized stocks, which are used as collateral to borrow USDC. That USDC is then lent out when expected lending rates are higher than the cost of borrowing. Holders keep their stock exposure, and any additional return comes from the gap between the two rates.

SuperStocks is Superform’s family of products built on tokenized equities and Earn Stocks is the strategy layer that puts the assets inside those products to work. Armitage’s role covers strategy design, allocation, risk management and ongoing monitoring. 

SuperformOS provides the operating system behind the products, bringing automated strategy execution, rule-based risk controls, accounting, and redemptions onto shared, verifiable infrastructure. 

“Putting a stock onchain is the starting point. The opportunity is building the financial products people use around it,” said Vikram Arun, CEO of Superform. “Superform brings together the infrastructure to run those products and the distribution to put them in investors’ hands. With Armitage, we’re bringing Wintermute’s strategy expertise into that system, starting with earning on stocks. Our ambition is to make SuperStocks the building blocks for a new generation of portfolios and investment products.”

For us, the opportunity is giving holders more options than just holding or selling their tokenized stocks,” said Igor Igamberdiev, Armitage Lead. “Putting those stocks to use onchain comes with real risks. Stock prices move, borrowing rates change, and positions need to be watched closely. That is the work we do every day, and we’re glad to be doing it with Superform.”

The collaboration covers eight existing SuperStocks products: NVIDIA, SpaceX, Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and Apple. Armitage is taking over as curator in stages, starting with the Amazon SuperVault (superAMZN). No new tokenized stocks are being issued.

Additional returns are variable and not guaranteed. Users can lose principal through market, borrowing-rate, liquidation, liquidity, oracle and smart-contract risks. Availability is subject to eligibility and applicable restrictions. This release is informational, not investment advice.

Eligible users can explore Earn Stocks and review SuperStocks product terms at https://app.superform.xyz/#stocks. 

About Superform

Superform is the neobank for global markets. Buy U.S. stocks, earn on USD, trade crypto, and send money without restrictions. Under the hood, SuperformOS connects financial products so users can move between investing, earning, and trading in fewer steps and earn more money, safely.

About Armitage

Armitage is Wintermute’s onchain vault curation arm, designed to scale across protocols and chains as yield opportunities emerge across an expanding DeFi landscape. Corto Industries Limited, is a company registered in the Cayman Islands (Company No. MC-434730), hereafter referred to as “Armitage”.

title: XRP Price Today: $1.03 Breakout Could Challenge Bearish Trend as XRP Trades Near $0.94
summary: XRP traded near $0.94 on November 24, recovering modestly after a sharp November decline, as traders monitored whether improving short-term momentum could challenge the broader bearish trend.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP traded near $0.94 on November 24, recovering modestly after a sharp November decline, as traders monitored whether improving short-term momentum could challenge the broader bearish trend.

The XRP price remains below major moving averages, with daily technical indicators showing persistent selling pressure. However, an emerging bullish signal on the four-hour chart and a potential recovery toward $1.03 have brought attention back to key resistance levels.

$1.03 Resistance Becomes Key Recovery Level

XRP was trading around $0.93–$0.94 on November 23, recording a daily recovery of approximately 1–2%. Despite the improvement, the cryptocurrency remains considerably below its late-September highs near $1.55, following a prolonged decline that pushed prices toward $0.90 in mid-November.

The $1.00–$1.20 range represents a critical short-term support and resistance zone for XRP on the daily chart. Source: @ChartNerdTA/X

TradingView’s daily technical summary maintains a Sell rating for XRP/USD, primarily because of bearish moving averages. All 12 major moving averages are signaling Sell, while oscillators present a more mixed picture.

The 10-period simple moving average (SMA) stands near $0.945, while the corresponding exponential moving average (EMA) is around $0.963. Both remain above the current XRP price, creating immediate resistance.

The 20-period SMA and EMA cluster near $1.03, making this area particularly important. A sustained move above that level could indicate improving market conditions and ease some of the immediate selling pressure.

Additional resistance remains between $1.08 and $1.12, followed by the 50-period moving averages around $1.16–$1.21. Longer-term averages extend toward $1.30, highlighting the distance XRP must recover before its broader technical structure improves.

ChartNerdTA has identified the $1.00–$1.20 region as a critical short-term trading range. The analyst cautioned that XRP previously experienced additional downside after failing to maintain this area, eventually reaching approximately $0.85.

The analyst’s Fibonacci analysis identifies resistance near $1.01 at the 0.236 retracement level, $1.11 at 0.382, and $1.21 at 0.5. These levels overlap with important moving averages, potentially creating several obstacles for buyers.

ChartNerdTA previously warned that XRP could experience a temporary rebound toward $1.00 before declining toward $0.89 or lower if it failed to reclaim the $1.03–$1.14 region.

XRP Shows First Bullish Signal on 4-Hour Chart Since November 6

While the daily chart continues to reflect a bearish structure, shorter-term indicators are showing early signs of improvement.

Crypto analyst @CW8900 identified the first bullish signal on XRP’s four-hour Binance perpetual futures chart since November 6. The development follows several weeks of downward movement, during which XRP declined from approximately $1.55 in late September to around $0.90 by mid-November.

The chart shows XRP falling from approximately $1.55 in late September to $0.90 in mid-November 2026, followed by a modest recovery and signs of a potential indicator reversal. Source: @CW8900/X

The latest chart shows a modest recovery alongside a potential reversal in the underlying technical indicator. This could indicate that selling momentum is beginning to weaken, although the signal alone does not establish a confirmed trend reversal.

Open interest has also declined, according to the chart shared by the analyst. Open interest measures the total number of outstanding futures contracts and provides insight into participation in derivatives markets.

A decline in open interest alongside a price recovery can reflect reduced exposure to leveraged positions rather than a clear increase in new bullish commitments. Additional confirmation from price action and derivatives activity would help establish whether the improvement has broader support.

TradingView’s shorter-timeframe readings offer a similar mixed picture. The one-hour technical summary leans toward Buy, while the four-hour timeframe remains Neutral. The daily and weekly readings, however, continue to indicate Sell or Strong Sell conditions.

This divergence suggests that XRP’s short-term recovery is developing within a broader bearish market structure rather than confirming a sustained change in direction.

XRP Price Prediction: Oversold Indicators Face Persistent Selling Pressure

Momentum indicators suggest XRP is approaching oversold territory, although they have yet to establish a convincing bullish reversal.

The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands near 31.1–31.4, just above the conventional oversold threshold of 30. Meanwhile, the Stochastic oscillator is around 26, and the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) is approximately -75.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The MACD remains negative near -0.088, reflecting the prevailing downward momentum, although some readings indicate improving short-term momentum relative to its signal line. The Awesome Oscillator and Momentum indicator also remain negative.

Together, these readings point to continued weakness alongside the possibility of a short-term relief rally. However, oversold conditions alone do not confirm that a market bottom has formed.

For the immediate trading session, the previous day’s pivot levels offer additional reference points. The classic pivot point stands near $0.925, with initial resistance at approximately $0.939, followed by $0.951 and $0.976.

On the downside, immediate support is positioned around $0.913–$0.914. A move below this area could expose the $0.899–$0.900 region, while a deeper decline may bring the $0.874 level into focus.

Recent price action also places additional support interest around $0.86–$0.90, an area that could become important if selling pressure returns.

A sustained recovery above $0.95 would provide an initial indication of improving short-term strength. A subsequent move toward $1.00 and the 20-period moving averages near $1.03 would offer a more meaningful test of the prevailing bearish trend.

XRP’s Multi-Year Triangle Puts Longer-Term Price Outlook in Focus

Beyond immediate resistance levels, ChartNerdTA has highlighted a broader technical structure involving XRP’s multi-year price history.

According to the analyst, XRP is approaching the apex of a third symmetrical triangle formation following a correction of approximately 76% in 2026. The chart examines nearly 13 years of price action and identifies repeated expansion and correction phases.

The 13-year chart highlights recurring XRP market cycles, with green expansion phases and Fibonacci projections indicating potential future price targets above $5. Source: @ChartNerdTA/X

ChartNerdTA described the current period as a pivotal “forge” moment, suggesting that maintaining the broader structure could establish a significant market low. Conversely, a breakdown from the formation would increase downside risks.

The analyst’s longer-term outlook includes potential price targets between $5 and $8 in 2027. These projections are based on historical expansion patterns and Fibonacci extensions displayed in the chart.

However, these targets remain conditional projections rather than established price levels. XRP would first need to stabilize, recover important technical resistance zones, and demonstrate sustained buying interest before such longer-term scenarios gain additional technical support.

For now, the immediate XRP price outlook remains closely tied to the $0.90 support region and the $1.03 resistance level. A successful recovery above the latter could weaken the current bearish structure, while renewed selling below $0.90 would keep downside risks in focus.

The developing four-hour bullish signal offers an early indication of improving momentum, but the daily moving averages continue to favor sellers. The next move around these key levels will help determine whether XRP is beginning a broader recovery or experiencing only a temporary rebound within its ongoing downtrend.

content:
MEXC is a global crypto exchange with very low trading fees, more than 3,000 listed digital assets, and high-leverage futures, but it is not licensed or available in every country. It serves over 40 million users across more than 170 countries. Still, people in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and several other blocked regions cannot open or use an account.

In this MEXC review, we will cover its fees, supported coins, futures trading, security features, KYC rules, and withdrawal process. You will also learn whether MEXC is safe in your country, who should use it, and which alternatives may suit you better.

What Is MEXC Global Crypto Exchange?

MEXC is a centralized crypto exchange that lets you buy, sell, hold, and trade digital assets from one account. The platform was launched back in 2018 under the name MXC Exchange, then rebranded to MEXC a couple of years later, and it has grown fast ever since.

You get access to spot markets, leveraged futures, savings products, and even a stock-trading arm called RealStocks, all inside one app or website. MEXC mainly built its name around altcoins. It lists new tokens faster than most big-name exchanges.

Now, below is a quick snapshot to give you a first glance at what MEXC actually offers:

Founded2018
Exchange TypeCentralized crypto exchange
User Reach40+ million users; 170+ markets claimed
Supported Coins3,000+ cryptocurrencies
Spot Fees0% maker; 0.05% taker
Futures Fees0% maker; 0.02% taker
Trading FeaturesSpot, futures, trading bots, copy trading, and P2P
Maximum LeverageUp to 200x in eligible regions
Withdrawal LimitsPrimary KYC: 80 BTC; Advanced KYC: 200 BTC daily
Crypto DepositsFree
Fiat OptionsCards, P2P, and third-party providers
Security Tools2FA, passkeys, anti-phishing code, withdrawal whitelist
Restricted RegionsUS, UK, Canada, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Kazakhstan, and others

What Are the Pros of MEXC?

The pros of MEXC are low trading fees, 3,000+ supported coins, copy trading, built-in bots, advanced futures tools, and published Proof of Reserves.

  • Zero-fee spot maker orders: You pay 0% on maker orders and just 0.05% on taker orders, well below the industry average.
  • Huge coin selection: You can find more than 3,000 crypto coins on MEXC. It has top coins like Bitcoin, but it also has low-cap tokens that you will not find on other platforms.
  • No mandatory KYC for basic use: You can sign up, deposit crypto, and trade spot or futures without submitting ID, at least up to a daily withdrawal limit (limits and no-KYC availability depend on region).
  • Copy trading and bots: The platform includes copy trading, grid bots, and DCA tools built right into the interface.
  • Advanced tools for futures: You get high leverage, hedge mode, cross or isolated margin, trailing stops, demo trading, and bots. Even BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT can reach 200x leverage in some eligible regions.
  • Proof of reserves: MEXC publishes reserve ratios that generally sit well above 100% for major assets like BTC, ETH, and USDT.

What Are the Cons of MEXC?

The cons of MEXC are limited regulatory approval, no direct bank withdrawals in most regions, possible risk-control freezes, third-party fiat services, and thin liquidity on some smaller coins.

  • No license in major markets: MEXC does not have approval from the SEC in the US, the FCA in the UK, or a MiCA license in Europe. Because of these missing licenses, nowadays, the platform completely blocks users from the US, UK, and Canada.
  • No direct bank withdrawal: You cannot send fiat straight to your bank account from MEXC in most regions, so cashing out takes an extra step through P2P or even a second exchange.
  • Risk-control freezes: Actually, some users report accounts getting locked for identity or fund-source review, which can hold up withdrawals for days.
  • Limited fiat on-ramps: Mostly, direct card and bank deposits go through third-party providers like Banxa, MoonPay, and Mercuryo rather than MEXC itself in many regions.
  • Thin liquidity on smaller listings: Some of the newest altcoins carry very thin order books, so a bigger order can easily move the price more than you would expect.

What Are the Fees on MEXC?

MEXC charges basic trading fees of 0% maker and 0.05% taker for spot trading, plus 0% maker and 0.02% taker for futures. Crypto deposits are completely free, while withdrawal fees can easily vary by coin and network, and some trading pairs may have different rates (based on active campaigns).

Spot Trading Fees

MEXC charges 0% in spot maker fees and 0.05% in spot taker fees for standard accounts. A maker order is the one that sits on the order book and waits to get filled, while a taker order is the one that matches instantly against an existing order. MX token holders receive a 20% fee reduction, and discounts apply to eligible spot trades as well.

Futures Trading Fees

MEXC charges a 0% futures maker fee and around 0.02% taker fees for futures trades. This rate can change a little bit based on the contract and where you live, and high volume traders may qualify for better pricing through tiered programs where available in their region. Also, funding rates settle every 8 hours on most pairs, and it usually range between 0.01% and 0.03%, either positive or negative.

Deposit & Withdrawal Fees

You do not have to pay any deposit fee when you add crypto to MEXC, no matter the coin or network. For crypto withdrawals, the fee depends on the specific coin and network you pick, and it goes up or down based on network traffic.

Fiat deposits and fiat purchases usually rely on third-party providers and can vary by region, provider fees, and processing times.

Well, a USDT withdrawal on the Tron network, for example, usually costs (1 USDT fee) far less than the same withdrawal on the Ethereum network (2-5 USDT fee), so picking the right chain easily saves you real money.

Are the Trading Fees on MEXC High?

No, MEXC’s trading fees rank among the lowest in the entire crypto exchange industry. A 0% maker fee on both spot and futures markets beats what Binance, Coinbase, and most other big platforms charge by default. Even the 0.05% spot taker fee and 0.02% futures taker fee sit well under typical industry averages, which often run close to double those numbers. Claims about zero fees mainly refer to maker pricing and occasional exchange promotions, not every trade type.

How to Reduce the MEXC Trading Fees?

You can reduce your MEXC fees in several ways, and the easiest one is simply placing limit orders instead of market orders. Limit orders count as maker orders most of the time, and maker orders cost 0% on both spot and futures. You can also use the MX token to reduce fees by 20% and use our referral code “mexc-bestbonus” to further reduce fees by 10%.

MX Token Fee Discounts

MX is MEXC’s native token, and mx token holders get a direct discount on trading fees. You get a 20% discount on spot and futures fees once the required MX balance is met, and discounts apply automatically with no extra step needed beyond holding the token.

Quick Note: MEXC suspended its older 50% fee discount for holding at least 500 MX. It is temporarily suspended.

MEXC Referral Code

The MEXC referral code “mexc-bestbonus” gives a new eligible user up to a 10% trading-fee discount and access to welcome tasks worth up to 10,000 USDT. You must enter the code while creating the account.

But remember, the full 10,000 USDT is not free cash. Actually, it requires KYC, deposit, and trading-volume tasks, and larger futures rewards usually come as credit you cannot withdraw directly. You can only withdraw profits.

Is MEXC Safe and Legit Globally?

Yes, MEXC is a safe and legit exchange that serves 40 million real traders, but “legit” here does not mean “fully regulated everywhere”. The platform runs real security infrastructure, publishes proof-of-reserves data, and has operated without a major hack since 2018. Still, it holds no top-tier license in the US, the UK, or under the EU’s MiCA framework, so your legal protection depends heavily on where you live.

Basically, MEXC is safe in the technical sense, meaning your funds face reasonable protection from hackers, but it is not “safe” in the regulatory sense the way a bank-backed or fully licensed exchange would be.

Also, there have been complaints about MEXC locking user funds through its risk control system. These freezes are mostly due to abnormal cryptocurrency trading activity in the user’s account.

Regulatory Status

MEXC does not hold any worldwide license that makes every service legal across 170+ markets. In fact, it is a highly unregulated exchange and operates without any license.

Note: MEXC also says it is registered with AUSTRAC in Australia, and in Europe, the exchange uses a local company called MEXC Estonia OÜ to handle some of its legal and compliance work. But again, we could not independently verify these claims, and it seems they are either false or the license is still pending.

Also, the exchange does not have a MiCA license in the EU. The rule deadline was July 1, 2026, so platforms without a license have to get approved or stop taking EU users. Because of this, things are still changing, and we still have to wait and see if people in Europe can use it.

MEXC is currently not available in the US, UK, Canada, Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Sudan, Kazakhstan, Russian-controlled parts of Ukraine, and high-risk areas. Plus, hiding your location can lead to account closure and forced liquidation.

So, is MEXC legit? Yes, it is a real exchange. Is it fully regulated globally? No. The difference between those two answers is important.

Available Security Features

MEXC’s available account security features are 2FA, passkeys, anti-phishing code, withdrawal address whitelist, and manual temporary account freeze.

  • Google Authenticator (2FA): You can link Google Authenticator to generate a new six-digit security code every 30 seconds, even without an internet connection. Generally, MEXC uses it as an extra check for sensitive actions such as logging in, trading, and withdrawing crypto.
  • Passkeys: MEXC supports passkeys that easily let you verify yourself using your fingerprint, face recognition, or device PIN instead of entering normal verification codes every time.
  • Anti-Phishing Code: You can create your own anti-phishing code, which MEXC then displays inside genuine emails sent to your account. Hence, it helps you identify fake emails.
  • Withdrawal Address Whitelist: You can turn on a withdrawal whitelist so crypto can only be sent to wallet addresses you have already approved. Also, MEXC even offers a security restriction that places a 24-hour waiting period on newly added whitelist addresses.
  • Account Freeze: MEXC lets you freeze your account quickly when you believe someone else has gained access to it.

Asset Protection

MEXC mainly backs user funds with a $100 million Guardian Fund. This one is built specifically to cover users if the platform ever suffers a hack or major technical failure, and MEXC says it also protects user assets through cold and hot wallet separation. Now, on top of that, the futures side runs its own risk reserve fund, which has held more than half a billion dollars in crypto assets.

MEXC also publishes monthly proof-of-reserves reports, and recent figures show reserve ratios staying pretty healthy, well above 100% for major coins. Hence, this means the exchange holds more crypto in reserve than users technically have on deposit.

What Are the Unique Trading Features of MEXC?

The unique trading features of MEXC are crypto spot trading, high-leverage perpetual futures, stock futures integration, automated bots, and copy trading.

Crypto Spot Trading

MEXC spot trading gives you access to one of the largest selections of cryptocurrencies among major centralized exchanges, with over 3,000 coins and a large range of spot pairs. Here, you can buy the actual crypto using pairs such as BTC/USDT or ETH/USDT, and the purchased coins then appear in your Spot wallet.

You can either place a market order when you want to buy or sell quickly, or use a limit order when you want to choose your own price. MEXC also gives you more order controls than just basic market and limit orders. The spot platform supports TP/SL, OCO, and trailing stop orders.

MEXC pairs its spot market with popular tools like grid bots and dollar-cost averaging, so even a beginner can easily automate a basic buy-low strategy without watching charts all day. The web platform is also easy to access from a browser if you prefer a desktop-style layout.

Crypto Perpetual Futures With High Leverage

MEXC’s futures market lets you trade over 900 perpetual contracts, with leverage reaching up to 200x on BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT pairs. Remember, altcoins have generally lower maximum leverage compared to BTC or ETH.

Currently, the exchange offers USDT-M, USDC-M, and Coin-M futures. USDT-M futures are the easiest to understand because you use USDT as both your margin and settlement currency.

Now, for USDC-M, you will be using USDC as a settlement currency, and for Coin-M, you will be using an underlying currency like BTC or ETH as a settlement currency. MEXC also supports cross margin and isolated margin, along with limit, market, trigger, and other advanced order types.

Stock Futures Integration

MEXC Stock Futures let you trade the price movement of major U.S. stocks directly from its futures platform. You can use crypto such as USDT as margin.

The trading platform currently offers stock futures linked to companies such as Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Coinbase, Robinhood, and McDonald’s, along with other available contracts.

Actually, MEXC uses the same general trading interface as its crypto perpetual futures, so the controls will already look familiar to you if you have used MEXC futures before. You can take both long and short positions, and some stock futures contracts even support leverage of up to 200x.

Automated & Copy Trading

MEXC offers many automated trading tools on desktop/browser access and its mobile apps. The main options include Spot Grid, Futures Grid, AI-assisted Futures Grid, and Futures Copy Trading.

Well, grid trading automatically places buy and sell orders inside a price range that you choose. Here, you need to set the upper price, lower price, number of grids, and investment amount, and the bot then tries to buy lower and sell higher as the market moves between those levels.

MEXC also provides futures grid trading, and you can run up to 10 futures grid bots at the same time. The feature currently works with USDT-M futures. Plus, its AI mode can study historical data to suggest the price range, number of grids, and leverage for you. User reviews often praise MEXC’s intuitive interface and easy navigation, while the app is also noted for stable, fast execution.

MEXC’s copy trading tool lets you automatically mirror the trades of experienced traders. You can compare traders using information such as ROI and PNL and then select the futures pairs you want to copy.

What Are MEXC Supported Cryptocurrencies and Trading Markets?

MEXC supports more than 3,000 digital assets along with many new altcoins and memecoins, and several crypto, futures, fiat, and stock-linked markets.

MEXC Supported Cryptocurrencies

MEXC supports major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Cardano, Dogecoin, Tron, and Litecoin. Plus, the stablecoins list includes USDT and USDC, while the wider list shows the exchange supports exposure to both mainstream assets and very new micro-cap projects across DeFi, meme coins, AI tokens, GameFi, Layer 1, Layer 2, DePIN, and real-world assets. Spot trading covers over 3,000 pairs, while the futures side runs more than 900 perpetual contracts. Many of these smaller tokens also appear on MEXC before they become widely accessible on decentralized exchanges.

MEXC Supported Trading Markets

MEXC’s supported markets span more than 170 countries, making it one of the most widely available crypto exchanges anywhere. Now, a specific set of jurisdictions stays fully blocked, though, and that list currently includes the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Singapore, alongside sanctioned states like North Korea, Iran, Cuba, and Sudan, plus several Russian-controlled regions of Ukraine. The European Union sits in a gray zone right now too, since MEXC holds no MiCA license.

How to Open a Trading Account on MEXC Crypto Exchanges

You can open a MEXC account by checking country eligibility, registering with an email or phone number, completing KYC, securing the account, and adding funds.

Step 1. Check your country first: You must not live in or access the exchange from a prohibited region. Plus, using a VPN to hide a blocked location breaks the “User Agreement” and can put withdrawals at risk.

Step 2. Open the official website or app: Visit the MEXC Global ltd official website, enter your email address or phone number, and create a unique password. Add the referral code as well. So, enter “mexc-bestbonus” in the referral field to link the fee discount and eligible new-user tasks. MEXC sends a one-time code to your email or phone. Enter it to finish the basic registration.

Step 3. Complete identity verification: Now, go to the “Identification” section in your account security tab. Select your country and document type, upload a clear ID, and finish the face check if the chosen level asks for it. You must also add security settings like 2FA, phishing codes, etc.

Step 4. Deposit or buy a small amount first: Go to the “Deposit” button under “Assets”, choose the exact coin and network on both platforms. We would suggest using a test transfer before moving a large balance. If supported, you can also deposit fiat currency under the “Buy Crypto” section.

Step 5. Place the first trade: Finally, you can visit the “Trade” section. Spot is the simpler starting point, and futures should wait until you understand margin, funding, liquidation price, and stop-loss orders.

Does MEXC Require KYC?

MEXC may or may not require KYC for trading, depending on your region. You see, MEXC used to be a no-KYC exchange, but nowadays, due to continuous regulatory scrutiny across regions, it has mandatory KYC verification in some countries (we were unable to get the exact list of countries). So, you may expect a KYC message if you are in highly regulated crypto countries.

Now, without KYC verification (wherever supported), MEXC has daily withdrawal limits of 10 BTC every 24 hours. You can increase your limit by completing either Primary or Advanced KYC, as higher limits generally require identity verification and may vary by region. Primary KYC allows withdrawals of up to 80 BTC within 24 hours, while Advanced KYC increases this limit to 200 BTC and includes additional features like OTC trading.

What Documents Are Required for KYC?

MEXC’s Primary KYC tier asks for a government-issued ID, like a passport, national ID card, or driver’s license.

Advanced KYC adds a proof of address requirement on top of that, usually a recent utility bill, bank statement, or official government letter dated within the last three months. Plus a live selfie to match your face against the document.

Also, institutional accounts need company registration paperwork and board-level documentation instead of personal ID. Every photo needs to be clear and unedited, since blurry or altered images are a common reason verification gets delayed or rejected.

How Long Does MEXC Verification Take?

MEXC verification normally finishes within about 15 minutes, but a review can take 8 to 24 hours. Actually, a busy market period, blurry image, data mismatch, unsupported document, or failed face scan can even make it slower.

Can You Withdraw Money From MEXC?

Yes, you can withdraw money from MEXC, though the process works a bit differently than a typical bank-linked exchange. If a withdrawal issue comes up, MEXC offers 24/7 customer support through live chat and email. You see, MEXC does not support direct fiat withdrawals to a bank account in most regions, so you need to either use the built-in P2P marketplace or move your crypto to a second exchange that does support bank withdrawals.

Now, through P2P, you must sell your crypto directly to another user who pays you through bank transfer, and MEXC holds the funds in escrow until both sides confirm the trade went through. The alternative route sends your crypto, usually a stablecoin like USDT, to an exchange such as Binance, Kraken, or Coinbase, where you sell it and then withdraw the cash straight to your bank. Some users also report delayed withdrawals, especially when compliance checks or P2P disputes are involved. Fiat support remains limited, and the exchange supports cash-out mainly through P2P or transfers to another platform rather than direct bank rails in most regions.

What Are the Alternatives to MEXC?

The best MEXC alternatives are Binance, Bybit, Coinbase, and Kraken. Here is a quick comparison:

ExchangeSupported CoinsBase Spot Fees (Maker/Taker)Futures TradingLicensed?Best Alternative in MEXC-Restricted Regions

Kraken350+0.40% / 0.80% at the starting tierYes, up to 50x in eligible non-US marketsYes, with 100+ licenses and registrations across 30+ countriesUS, UK, and Canada

Who Should Use MEXC?

You should use MEXC if you want access to a large altcoin selection, low trading fees, high-leverage futures, copy trading, built-in trading bots, and other unique features.

  • Altcoin traders: MEXC is really a good fit for you if you mainly look for early access to smaller or newer cryptocurrencies. As discussed earlier, the exchange lists thousands of spot trading pairs, so you get more choice than on many larger regulated platforms.
  • Futures traders: You can prefer MEXC if you actively trade perpetual futures and want access to high leverage. Well, some selected BTC and ETH contracts can offer leverage of up to 200x.
  • Active traders looking for low fees: MEXC can work well if you trade frequently and want to keep trading costs very low. Its standard spot and futures fees are very low compared to other exchanges like Binance or Bitget, and some spot campaigns offer zero fees on eligible pairs.
  • Traders who use bots or copy trading: MEXC is useful if you want to automate part of your trading instead of placing every order yourself. You can use grid bots, AI-assisted futures grid tools, and copy trading from the same account.
  • Professional traders who want more market choices: MEXC suits experienced traders who want access to spot, futures, stock futures, and advanced order types in one place, and it can also appeal if you want extras like a token issuance platform and occasional token sales alongside the main exchange. Basically, you get a lot of advanced tools, but the platform can feel a bit much for someone completely new to crypto.

Now, who should avoid MEXC? Mainly, beginners who want strong consumer protections, direct bank withdrawals, and a fully regulated home base in the US or UK, though, should probably look elsewhere, since MEXC simply is not built for that kind of user; beginners looking for demo accounts that mirror live markets may also prefer a more education-first setup.

title: Quant (QNT) Price Today: QNT Rebounds 6% With Bullish RSI Divergence as Exchange Supply Hits Yearly Low
summary: Quant (QNT) has rebounded nearly 6% in 24 hours, recovering from recent lows near $137 as bullish RSI divergence and declining exchange reserves draw attention to improving market conditions.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: QNT

Quant (QNT) has rebounded nearly 6% in 24 hours, recovering from recent lows near $137 as bullish RSI divergence and declining exchange reserves draw attention to improving market conditions.

However, the Quant price remains below several key moving averages, leaving its short-term recovery without a confirmed trend reversal.

QNT was trading around $145–$147 on November 23, following a November 21 decline to approximately $127. The recovery coincides with a rise in wallet holders and a reported drop in exchange balances to a yearly low. Together, these developments offer a more constructive on-chain picture, although technical resistance continues to limit the upside.

QNT Price Today: Bullish RSI Divergence Emerges After Sharp Decline

Quant’s four-hour chart shows a potential shift in momentum after an extended period of selling. According to TradingView analyst BKVIP, QNT has formed a bullish Relative Strength Index (RSI) divergence across its latest three price lows.

Quant is trading near $145 after rebounding from the November 21 low of $127, with bullish RSI divergence emerging following a sharp decline. Source: BKVIP on TradingView

The divergence developed as QNT declined from the $150 region to approximately $139 on November 15 and then to $127 on November 21. During the same period, the RSI formed progressively higher lows near 22, 24, and 27. This contrast suggests that selling momentum weakened even as the token continued to establish lower prices.

The RSI subsequently recovered toward 46 as QNT bounced from its November 21 low. This development indicates improving short-term momentum, but it does not independently confirm a trend reversal.

QNT’s broader four-hour structure remains bearish. The token reached approximately $224 in late October before forming lower highs near $210 and $205 in early November. Selling pressure subsequently pushed the price below $170 and $150.

At the time of the latest market assessment, QNT was testing the $142–$147 region. The $145 area represents an immediate technical hurdle, while the $148–$150 range aligns with nearby resistance from short-term moving averages.

A sustained move above $145, followed by a reclaim of $157, would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. Such a move could expose the $162 and $169 resistance levels.

Conversely, a decline below $127 would weaken the bullish divergence setup. The $120 psychological level would then become a potential downside reference.

Exchange Supply Falls to Yearly Low as QNT Holders Approach 200K

On-chain developments are providing another point of interest for Quant investors. Crypto analyst Tokenicer reported that QNT balances held on cryptocurrency exchanges have declined to a new yearly low, indicating that fewer tokens are currently sitting on trading platforms.

QNT exchange reserves have fallen to a new yearly low, with balances declining sharply toward the end of 2026. Source: @Tokenicer/X

A reduction in exchange balances can reflect a shift toward self-custody or longer-term holding. It may also reduce the amount of QNT immediately available for sale on exchanges. However, exchange outflows alone do not establish investor accumulation, as wallet transfers and custody arrangements can also influence these figures.

Holder statistics show a corresponding increase in the number of QNT addresses. Ethereum mainnet data recorded approximately 189,549 holders during November 13–19, compared with around 167,000 in early September. This represents an increase of approximately 13%, or more than 21,000 additional addresses.

The growth followed Quant’s September 24 announcement involving The Clearing House and its On-Chain Money Initiative. The partnership selected Quant to provide technology for an interoperable network designed to support the clearing and settlement of tokenized deposits among financial institutions.

QNT wallet holders have increased sharply since late September, with nearly 21,000 new wallets added following the September 24, 2026, Clearing House partnership announcement. Source: @Tokenicer/X

The initiative focuses on connecting tokenized deposit transactions with existing financial infrastructure. Quant’s technology is expected to provide interoperability, orchestration, and transaction-management capabilities, including connectivity to The Clearing House’s RTP and CHIPS payment networks.

The Clearing House’s Chief Strategy Officer, Sal Karakaplan, said, “Building interbank infrastructure for tokenized deposits requires proven technology that can scale.”

The network is expected to become available to participating financial institutions in the first half of 2027. Although the partnership represents a development in Quant’s institutional infrastructure business, the increase in QNT wallet addresses does not establish that the announcement directly caused the holder growth.

Together, the declining exchange balances and expanding holder count provide useful context for assessing QNT’s on-chain activity. Nevertheless, these metrics should be considered alongside trading volume, price action, and broader market conditions rather than treated as independent indicators of an impending rally.

QNT Price Analysis: $157 Resistance Remains Critical

Despite the recent recovery, Quant’s daily technical structure continues to show signs of weakness. QNT remains below most short- and medium-term moving averages, suggesting that sellers still have influence over the broader price trend.

The 10-day simple moving average stands near $148, while the 20-day and 50-day averages are considerably higher, around $166 and $192, respectively. The corresponding exponential moving averages also remain above the current market price, creating additional resistance between approximately $150 and $169.

The daily RSI is around 38, reflecting subdued momentum without indicating an extremely oversold market. Meanwhile, the MACD remains in negative territory, suggesting that bearish momentum has not fully disappeared. The Stochastic oscillator, however, is approaching oversold territory and offers a more constructive short-term signal.

Longer-term indicators present a different picture. QNT continues to trade above its 200-day simple moving average near $106 and its 200-day exponential moving average around $125. These levels provide a longer-term reference for potential support, although they do not guarantee that the recent decline has ended.

On the upside, $145 represents the first important resistance area, followed by $148–$150. A sustained move above this region could bring $157 into focus. This level is particularly important because reclaiming it would challenge the sequence of lower highs that has defined the recent four-hour downtrend.

If buyers overcome $157, the next resistance levels stand near $162 and $169. A recovery toward $169 would represent a more substantial improvement in market structure and suggest that the recent bullish divergence is translating into stronger price action.

On the downside, the $137–$143 region remains an important support area. A breakdown below $137 could expose the $125–$130 zone, where longer-term moving averages and the lower Bollinger Band provide additional technical reference points.

The November 21 low near $127 remains the most important level for the four-hour bullish divergence setup. A decisive move below it would invalidate the current pattern and weaken the case for a near-term recovery. Further downside could then bring the psychological $120 level into view.

title: Trump’s Meme Coin Dinner Exposes a 94% Collapse in Holder Commitments
summary: Key takeaways Wallets on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held about $9.1 million at the November 16 cutoff, against roughly $148 million for the first dinner in May 2025, a drop of close to 94% in visible dollar value. That does not mean 94% of investors withdrew cash: the token price fell sh...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Wallets on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held about $9.1 million at the November 16 cutoff, against roughly $148 million for the first dinner in May 2025, a drop of close to 94% in visible dollar value.
  • That does not mean 94% of investors withdrew cash: the token price fell sharply, and the two leaderboards are not identical in size or method.
  • The top 10 wallets held about 81% of the tokens on the public board, and the top 29 about 95%.
  • Public Citizen traced 66 of the 130 displayed wallets to exchanges that restrict US customers, which is not proof about who attended.

Donald Trump’s latest meme coin dinner came with a striking financial comparison: wallets displayed on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held approximately $9.1 million in tokens at the November 16 cutoff, compared with roughly $148 million associated with the first dinner in May 2025. That puts the decline in the publicly measured dollar value at close to 94%. It does not mean investors withdrew 94% of their cash, or that 94% fewer people turned up for dinner.

Trump hosted the third event for major $TRUMP holders at his Virginia golf club on Sunday, November 22. The gathering itself was new, but the more interesting story is what the leaderboard reveals about a token that was once able to turn a private invitation into a market-wide buying contest. NewsBTC previously covered an earlier $TRUMP meme coin dinner rally. This time, the numbers tell a considerably less flattering story about the value attached to that privilege.

What the 94% Figure Actually Measures

The roughly $9.1 million estimate comes from Public Citizen’s November 22 review of the 130 wallets displayed on the final public leaderboard. Its researchers counted 9,794,832.87 $TRUMP tokens and valued them at approximately $0.93 each at the November 16, 9 a.m. Eastern cutoff. The older $148 million comparison refers to the first gala’s leaderboard in May 2025.

# Name Wallet Time-weighted holdings Latest $TRUMP balance Days held
1 FastX Dd54…uHDD 1,389,617.57 1,771,794.76 39.45
2 few DNLo…EoY6 1,093,044.76 1,000,000.00 35.75
3 Unitas Mhgx…itas 997,566.73 1,241,671.11 46.33
4 taotao BWgb…drJH 984,339.81 1,147,626.05 40.20
5 Yulia Gzyw…d6cp 966,503.35 1,126,182.24 40.23
6 GoTrump 3MwE…R1oS 453,211.23 459,963.62 46.34
7 FASTXCO H1fu…hh1c 436,614.04 700,002.00 29.24
8 ymca 8TUd…kg3S 137,348.63 140,000.96 45.98
9 3Eye 8DHk…qRjW 117,063.01 200,000.00 27.43
10 cl16 FNUY…Mts9 118,840.61 122,552.25 45.45

Source: Official $TRUMP Gala Dinner Leaderboard (November 16, 2026). Rankings based on time-weighted token holdings. Wallet entries do not necessarily represent individual attendees.

That works out to a decline of roughly 93.9%, rounded to 94%. But the events did not have identical leaderboard sizes or necessarily identical valuation methods. More importantly, the token’s price fell dramatically between the two events. A lower marked-to-market balance can reflect falling prices even if some holders retain comparable token quantities.

Calling this a 94% collapse in new investment would therefore be wrong. The narrower conclusion is still hard to ignore: the value represented by the public competition for dinner access is a small fraction of what it was at the first event.

The leaderboard also should not be mistaken for a headcount. While the public display showed 130 wallets, organizers said 185 wallets qualified under the event’s rules. One person can control multiple wallets, and a wallet can be held for an organization. Neither figure identifies exactly who attended Sunday night’s dinner.

A Few Wallets Still Control Most of the Leaderboard

The smaller overall value is only part of the picture. Public Citizen found that the top 10 wallets held about 81% of the tokens on the public board. The top 29 accounted for approximately 95%. Those top-ranked wallets were also eligible for a special VIP reception.

The concentration matters because a leaderboard is marketed as a contest between investors, but its aggregate value can be dominated by a very small number of positions. Looking at the $9.1 million as if it represented broad, evenly distributed enthusiasm would be as misleading as treating all 130 wallet entries as separate people.

There is a revealing detail near the bottom of Public Citizen’s review: the wallet ranked No. 130 held only 9.71 $TRUMP, worth about $9 at the snapshot. It qualified because the competition measured time-weighted holdings over the scoring period, rather than the balance left in the wallet at the very end. That is perfectly compatible with the rules. It also shows why a dinner ranking cannot be read as a simple list of fresh purchases or long-term conviction.

There is another market point here. A buyer who wants dinner access can acquire the token and hedge some of the price risk elsewhere. Holding a spot position long enough to earn a place does not necessarily make someone a directional believer in the coin. In that sense, the competition measures an incentive to qualify, not a clean vote of confidence in future returns.

The Wallet Trail Raises Questions, Not Conclusions About Guests

Public Citizen’s researchers traced 66 of the 130 displayed wallets, or 51%, to direct transfers from exchanges that restrict US customers. Those wallets represented about 4.35 million $TRUMP, roughly 44% of the public board’s token holdings. Among the top 29 VIP-ranked wallets, 15 had received tokens directly from such exchanges, according to the group’s November 22 findings.

That is useful on-chain information. It is not proof that 66 dinner guests were foreign nationals, that all those exchanges served prohibited customers, or that any particular attendee broke a rule. An exchange withdrawal identifies a source of tokens, not a passport or the identity of the person controlling the receiving wallet. Public Citizen put a basic transparency problem plainly: “The names of the invitees have not been disclosed.” That sentence matters because a wallet address, however transparent its transaction history, cannot supply the accountability that a named guest list would provide.

The event’s official website states:

“

GetTrumpMemes.com is not political and has nothing to do with any political campaign or any political office or governmental agency.

That is the organizers’ characterization. It does not remove the transparency question created when holders of a president-linked digital asset can compete for personal access to the president. Neither does that question, by itself, prove an improper exchange of favors.

The Dinner Still Has Value. The Token’s Investment Case Is Another Matter.

There is a credible bullish counterargument. An exclusive dinner is a limited, experience driven reward. Its value to attendees need not move in lockstep with the coin’s market capitalization, and falling token prices can make it cheaper for new participants to qualify. The gala went ahead, and its promoters continue to offer other experiences to holders.

But that is precisely why we should be careful about treating an invitation contest as evidence of a durable investment base. Access is an incentive. It is not a claim on business earnings, and it does not put a floor under the price of the coin.

The most uncomfortable part of this comparison for $TRUMP holders is not that the dinner was smaller or less glamorous. The available figures do not establish either claim. It is that the token’s most recognizable promotional feature remains personal access, while the dollar value visible on the public leaderboard has fallen dramatically since the first event.

In our view, that weakens the argument that repeated celebrity events, by themselves, can sustain the market’s appetite for the token. A more persuasive sign of recovering demand would be durable, independently observable holdings beyond a contest period, with less dependence on a few top-ranked wallets. The next useful data would be post-event wallet balances and exchange flows, measured against the November 16 snapshot, not just another photograph from the dinner.

For now, the 94% comparison is a warning about the dollar value of the visible leaderboard, not proof of a 94% investor exodus. That distinction makes the story more credible, and no less troubling for anyone relying on the dinner promotion as an investment thesis.

title: HAN CHAIN Schedules Launch of Its First Flagship Project, ARGO, for December 18, 2026
summary: Athens, Greece, 23rd November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Athens, Greece, 23rd November 2026, Chainwire

Athens, Greece, November 23rd, 2026, Chainwire

HAN CHAIN Schedules Launch of Its First Flagship Project, ARGO, for December 18, 2026

HAN CHAIN (Human-Centered AI Network) plans to launch its first flagship project, ARGO, on December 18, 2026. HAN CHAIN aims to build a public blockchain for the quantum computing era, with post-quantum cryptography and on-chain security as research and development priorities. ARGO brings digital computing power, on-chain accounts, and online learning activities together in a web platform.

ARGO Launch Scope

The ARGO website offers two entry points: Expedition for wallet-based computing features and Exploration for email-based access to learning activities.

In Expedition, users can connect a wallet on BNB Chain, register an on-chain account, and view their computing power and purchase history in the Holdings section. Presale participants can use this section to review the account and computing power associated with their connected wallet. Users confirm on-chain transactions in their wallets.

In Exploration, users can sign up by email and participate in learning activities. They can start with those activities and connect a wallet later if they choose to use Expedition.

Presale Close and Computing Activation

ARGO’s 45-day computing power presale is scheduled to end on December 18, 2026, the same day as the planned launch. During the presale, users can purchase computing power using USDT on BNB Chain.

Under the schedule published on the ARGO website, computing activation is planned for December 19, 2026, at 00:00 local time in Greece. Once the system is activated, eligible computing power is scheduled to begin generating DE under the platform’s published rules. DE (Discovery Economy) is ARGO’s ecosystem token, and its use is governed by official project documentation.

The presale and computing activation announcement is available in the News section of the ARGO website. Users can check their computing power status under Expedition → Holdings.

About HAN CHAIN

HAN CHAIN is pursuing the development of a public blockchain for the quantum computing era. Its research priorities include post-quantum cryptography and on-chain security, with a focus on how public blockchains can protect account identities, digital signatures, and transaction verification as quantum computing advances. ARGO currently uses BNB Chain for on-chain accounts and presale transactions.

ARGO is HAN CHAIN’s first flagship project, combining digital computing power, Web3 applications, and learning activities. HAN CHAIN is also developing HANMEET, a project focused on browser-based meetings and online collaboration.
