title: Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading
summary: Key takeaways The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit is estimated at $5.7 million across two stages, according to SlowMist, which is not an audited final total. About $1.87 million in proceeds was traced to the attacker, while 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued near $3.7 million, were reportedly with...
content:
Key takeaways

  • The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit is estimated at $5.7 million across two stages, according to SlowMist, which is not an audited final total.
  • About $1.87 million in proceeds was traced to the attacker, while 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued near $3.7 million, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge.
  • Bithumb halted ACE trading on November 23 after finding signs that abnormally issued ACE had entered exchanges.
  • In the material reviewed, Fusionist has not published a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem.

The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit has produced an estimated $5.7 million in losses across two stages, according to SlowMist’s incident tracker. After unbacked ACE tokens were minted on BNB Chain and sold, traders reportedly used the resulting price collapse to withdraw real ACE from the project’s Endurance bridge reserves. The fallout reached centralized exchanges on Monday, November 23: Bithumb halted ACE trading after finding indications that abnormally issued tokens had entered crypto exchanges.

This was not one attacker walking away with $5.7 million in a single transaction. The distinction matters. Roughly $1.87 million was traced through the attacker’s proceeds, while another 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued around $3.7 million at the incident’s reference prices, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. SlowMist lists a combined $5.7 million loss estimate, not an audited final total. The bridge’s most basic promise, that a token issued on one chain corresponds to something real on another, is precisely what now needs proving.

A Privileged Minter Printed Tokens That Had No Backing

Security firm Blockaid flagged the Fusionist bridge-minter exploit on November 22. Its alert described the mechanism bluntly:

“

A privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT.

The firm initially estimated that about $1.04 million had been extracted while the attack was still ongoing. That was an interim snapshot, not a cap on the damage.

Blockchain-monitoring account Onchain Lens subsequently reported that an attacker had routed 1,091.5 ETH, valued at about $1.87 million at the time, through Tornado Cash. That observation traces a movement of proceeds, not an extra $1.87 million to add on top of the initial extraction estimate. The values describe different points in the same suspected attacker’s fund flow.

Fusionist acknowledged an apparent ongoing ACE exploit on BNB Smart Chain on Sunday and asked users to suspend transfers, trading and bridging on that network. It has not, in the material reviewed, provided a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem identifying how the privileged minting authority was abused.

A bridge minter is supposed to create a token representation only when the corresponding value is properly accounted for. Once the right to mint is misused, a chain can show perfectly ordinary-looking balances that have no matching backing.

It is a familiar failure mode: NewsBTC previously covered a bridge-role exploit that minted unbacked tokens at CrediX. That earlier case does not establish Fusionist’s root cause, but it illustrates why elevated bridge permissions are such a consequential security boundary.

Traders Found a Second Exit Through Real ACE Reserves

The subsequent drain may prove more important than the initial minting spree.

According to SlowMist’s November 22 incident entry, traders bought the sharply discounted ACE created by the market disruption and used the cross-chain bridge to withdraw about 53.7 million genuine ACE from the Endurance-side reserves. SlowMist valued that withdrawal at approximately $3.7 million.

Here is the mechanism without the jargon. A representation of ACE on BNB Chain suddenly became cheap because unauthorized supply had flooded the market. A bridge that would still accept those tokens in exchange for ACE on Endurance offered an obvious difference in value.

Anyone able to complete that conversion could receive real tokens in return for deeply discounted ones. The trading opportunity existed because the backing and the circulating representation were no longer in a trustworthy relationship.

The $3.7 million figure is a valuation of the ACE reserve outflow, not proof that every recipient sold those tokens for $3.7 million in cash. Nor does it mean every trader involved helped compromise the minter.

There is a meaningful difference between initiating the security breach and trading through a system whose defenses have already failed.

Those distinctions should not obscure the core problem. A bridge can have technically valid transactions and still produce an economically disastrous result. If unbacked supply can be redeemed for genuine reserves, the checks have failed where they matter most.

Bithumb’s Monday Halt Shows How Far the Problem Travelled

Bithumb suspended ACE deposits and withdrawals early on November 23. It then halted trading effective 7:30 a.m. Korea time, according to its follow-up ACE security notice.

The exchange said, in a translation from its Korean announcement, that it had:

“

confirmed indications that abnormally issued ACE had entered cryptocurrency exchanges.

It identified two related BNB Chain transactions and a second transaction.

Those records are important evidence leads, but a full independent decoding of the transaction trail remains outstanding.

Bithumb’s wording is careful: it reported signs of abnormal supply entering exchanges, not a finding that every ACE token in customer accounts is invalid. The trading suspension is a protective response, not a finalized determination of customer losses.

Still, it creates a practical problem for holders who never used the bridge. If tokens are fungible within a market, exchanges and the issuer need a credible method for identifying affected supply and deciding how deposits, balances and trades will be treated.

The Real Security Question Is Why the Bridge Could Honor the Claims

There is an understandable temptation to focus on the enormous minting figures. The more consequential question is what happened when those tokens met the bridge’s reserves.

A system does not need to lose control of its entire blockchain to suffer a serious failure in one privileged contract role. Nor should a successful-looking bridge transaction count as evidence that the asset being transferred was fully backed.

Our assessment

The response cannot end with a pause notice and a promise to investigate.

Fusionist needs to show which minting permissions were affected, whether they have been revoked, how much ACE was created without backing, how the Endurance-side reserve changed and what claims remain outstanding.

Exchanges need a defensible token-treatment plan, and holders need to know whether there is a shortfall and who is responsible for covering it.

There is a fair counterargument: the $5.7 million figure is an external estimate, market prices moved during the incident, and the precise compromise method is not established.

SlowMist categorizes the incident as private-key leakage, but that classification is not a substitute for an official technical finding. It would also be premature to treat a cautious exchange halt as proof that every affected customer suffered a loss.

Those qualifications change how the numbers should be reported. They do not make the underlying bridge-accounting failure less serious.

The next credible milestone is not a restored interface or a reassuring social post. It is a transparent reconciliation of the tokens minted, the reserves withdrawn and the assets still available to back legitimate ACE claims.

Until that exists, the estimated $5.7 million fallout remains a warning about both token security and the risks of trusting a bridge’s accounting.

title: Fusionist ACE Exploit Drains Over $2M, Attacker Sends 1,150 ETH Into Tornado Cash
summary:
Key Takeaways: An ACE exploit in Fusionist resulted in a loss of over $2 million. The attacker purposefully issued and created bogus ACE at multiple sites. Approximately $1.97 million (1,150
The post Fusionist ACE Exploit Drains Over $2M, Attacker Sends 1,150 ETH Into Tornado Cash appeared first on ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • An ACE exploit in Fusionist resulted in a loss of over $2 million.
  • The attacker purposefully issued and created bogus ACE at multiple sites.
  • Approximately $1.97 million (1,150 ETH) was transferred to Tornado Cash.

The discovery of a massive exploit in Fusionist’s ACE ecosystem has led to an increase of unearthing unauthorized tokens for selling them purchases of crypto assets after taking over the privilege of creating tokens.

On-chain data tracked by Lookonchain shows the attacker later converted proceeds into Ether and moved a substantial portion through Tornado Cash.

Fusionist (@fusionistio) was hacked for over $2M!

The attacker minted and dumped a large amount of $ACE, sending some to Gate, MEXC, and Baltex to sell.

The attacker then swapped the funds for $ETH and has already deposited 1,150 $ETH ($1.97M) into #TornadoCash.

https://t.co/lqtxIeUCKb

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 23, 2026

  • Fusionist ACE Exploit Triggers Heavy Token Dump
  • 1,150 ETH Moves Into Tornado Cash
    • Bridge Liquidity Faces a Second Shock
    • Fusionist Has Yet to Publish a Full Post-Mortem

Fusionist ACE Exploit Triggers Heavy Token Dump

The hacker managed to mint and resell a massive number of ACE, some of which were offered on exchanges such as Gate, MEXC, and Baltex, according to Lookonchain. The cross-chain staker doesn’t seem to have been compromised as much as Fusionist’s cross-chain bridge infrastructure.

Separate blockchain analysis indicates the attacker abused a privileged minting role linked to the ACE bridge on BNB Chain, allowing unbacked tokens to be created and sold into available liquidity. Users were then instructed by Fusionist to suspend ACE transfers, trading and bridging on BSC while investigations were conducted.

Read More: Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Signing System

1,150 ETH Moves Into Tornado Cash

The attacker sold the newly-minted ACE and used those proceeds to buy back ETH.

Lookonchain mentioned that already 1,150 ETH with a value of approximately $1.97 million have already been sent to the crypto mixer Tornado Cash, which is often utilized to cover up the tracks of transactions.

The on-chain relationship between funds received by users and withdrawn by them will be affected by the mixing of funds in and out, which will create additional complications for recovery.

There have been a few slight variations in estimates by other trackers. Onchain Lens, for example, traced about 1,091.5 ETH worth roughly $1.87 million through Tornado Cash. The discrepancy is due to different tracking windows and not a change in the underlying exploit; it is not an actual change.

Bridge Liquidity Faces a Second Shock

The first one posed another issue for Fusionist’s bridge. After ACE collapsed on BNB Chain, traders were able to buy the heavily discounted tokens and bridge them into Fusionist’s Endurance network, where the system released real ACE reserves.

About 53.7 million ACE, valued at approximately $3.7 million, were left out of the Endurance-side bridge before the reserves were almost depleted, the Block reported. This was aside from the attacker’s initial $2 million haul.

In response to the exchange actions reported following the incident, Gate has suspended spot trades in ACE/USDT and limited its ACE perpetual market.

Fusionist Has Yet to Publish a Full Post-Mortem

Fusionist, when the latest reports were issued, admitted to an ongoing exploit but urged users not to interact with ACE on BSC, but did not provide the fault analysis as to how privileged minting access was acquired.

It is still worth noting: there’s evidence of something messing up at the bridge level, but the reason Fusionist has not yet made a public statement.

title: GTA VI Has Better Taste Than Your Discover Weekly
summary: Stockyard FM, a radio station in a fictional Florida, remembers something the streaming services can only approximate. Sometimes the best record is the one you wouldn’t have chosen for yourself.
content:
Skip to content

Stockyard FM, a radio station in a fictional Florida, remembers something the streaming services can only approximate. Sometimes the best record is the one you wouldn’t have chosen for yourself.

The record that sells me on Stockyard FM is LCD Soundsystem’s “North American Scum.” If you’re going to put a song about the embarrassment of being American in a game that sells the rest of the world a fantasy of being American, that’ll do nicely. You could put it under a shot of a beautiful condo rising behind a petrol station and get most of the way through an essay about Florida before the first chorus. On the same station are Caribou’s “Never Come Back” and Fischerspooner’s “Emerge.” Someone was willing to let those three tastes sit in the same car. Rockstar’s credits have The Dare playing Harrison and PinkPantheress playing Victoria on the mic.

LCD Soundsystem’s official video for “North American Scum,” one of the tracks on Stockyard FM.

I’d be perfectly happy if Discover Weekly put any of those records in my Monday queue. That’s part of my problem with it. I’m a dangerously easy man to please if you know which ten songs I’ve played to death. Eventually a playlist made from my habits starts to resemble the cupboard I open every night expecting it to contain something different.

What the DJ heard in it

Played on their own, those Stockyard records get filed under different moods. “Emerge” has the hard, slightly ridiculous glamour of electroclash. Caribou is warmer, a dance record that keeps drawing you back to the same phrase. LCD Soundsystem turns a national identity crisis into something you can shout along to. The station makes room for the joke, the mood and the beat. The connection makes sense once someone makes it for you, which is a big part of the pleasure of hearing somebody else pick records.

Put three good records in a folder and you have three good records. Put the wrong one on at the right moment and people will ask you what it was. Anyone who’s played records to a room knows the next ten minutes can change how the previous ten sounded. A person walking onto the dance floor has to decide whether they trust you. Give them everything they already wanted and you’ll probably have a pleasant night. One person might even remember it.

The original Vice City understood this well enough that Rockstar and Sony released seven soundtrack albums in 2002, each built around a station. You could take that fictional station home without the driving or the cops. Years later, Rockstar’s music director Ivan Pavlovich, who founded the Chicago deep-house label Guidance Recordings, explained how the studio worked on GTA V. “We license way more music than we use,” he told The Guardian. Anyone who’s come home from a record shop with a stack of good records and then left half of them in the bag before a set knows that feeling. Choosing what to leave out is a large part of the job.

As requested by your previous self

Spotify says Discover Weekly had generated more than 100 billion track streams by its tenth anniversary in 2025. In the anniversary post, it calls the selections “handpicked just for them.” The service has put plenty of people onto artists they would never have heard otherwise. Ordinarily I’m delighted when a computer turns up a useful record and requires nothing in return beyond knowing a disturbing amount about my Tuesday nights.

But Spotify’s two important words there are for them. Its promise is that my next discovery will fit me. Stockyard FM serves a different purpose. A player who found Fischerspooner last week and someone who bought the single when it came out can turn on the same station. The records sound different to each person. They have something to talk about anyway.

What Rockstar has at its disposal is context Spotify can only guess at. The scenery and the soundtrack inhabit the same world. “North American Scum” has a different job playing in a car in Vice City than it has as the fourth song on a playlist called Indie Dance Party. One of the cheapest ways to change a scene in a film is to change the record under it. Radio lets a player blunder into the same effect on the way to a petrol station.

Of course, Rockstar has a commercial use for all of this. There’s a separate 34-track album of original music to stream or buy. BNC has already covered what the company sold you in the game box. It’s perfectly possible to enjoy the radio while noticing that the record shop and the car dealership have the same owner.

Still, I’m glad somebody in Vice City is prepared to put on a record I might turn off. For a song to change your mind, there has to be a moment when you’re pretty sure it won’t. Give it until the next set of lights.

Telegram crypto signals are trading tips sent through Telegram groups by expert traders to help people buy or sell cryptocurrencies at the right time. The signals contain information such as what cryptocurrency to buy/sell, entry-level, take-profits, and stop-loss points to limit risks. 

Telegram is widely used for this reason since it’s quick, safe, and updates can be exchanged instantly within the groups. There are free groups and paid ones, with the paid groups containing additional features such as additional signals, technical analysis, and one-to-one assistance.

How to Choose the Best Crypto Signals Group?

The factors to consider when choosing the best crypto signals group are a high win rate, strong market analysis, experienced traders, a balanced number of signals, proper risk management, clear and fast communication, transparent and fair pricing, and a supportive community for learning.

  • High Win Rate: A good crypto signals group must have a minimum of 70% win rate. Seven out of ten trades must be winners. Most groups boast high accuracy, but few offer actual evidence. Looking at past results helps verify whether the group is genuine. Verified track records indicate actual performance. Groups that conceal previous signals typically have something to hide. The best crypto Telegram groups deliver actual profits and do not merely promote fake success to get new members.
  • Market Analysis: A crypto signals group should not only inform you when to sell and buy. It should inform you why a trade is worth taking. Good analysis provides market trends, levels of resistance and support, and risk aspects. A team that sends you signals without rationale is useless. You learn more as a trader if you learn why each trade was made.
  • Seasoned Traders Run the Group: Seasoned traders always know price action, trends, and risk control. They have years of experience in profitable trading. Most groups are operated by newbies or marketers who do not understand actual trading. An efficient group is run by experts who share their information. They let you know the reason why a signal is given rather than leaving random entries. 
  • Balanced Number of Signals: A reliable crypto signals group provides 2-5 good quality signals a day. Too many signals result in overtrading and losses. Quality is always preferred over quantity while trading. 
  • Risk Management: A stop-loss and take-profit should always be offered by a signals group. Crypto trading without a stop-loss brings large losses. Also, risk-to-reward ratios must be included in the signals. Having a good risk-to-reward setup guarantees that gains are greater than losses over time. 
  • Clear and Quick Communication: A group should offer clear messages for every trade. Delayed or unclear messages lead to the loss of opportunities by traders. An efficient group provides information regarding live trades and market updates. In a volatile market, fast updates enable traders to make good choices, and bad communication results in losses since traders have no idea when to close or modify their trades. 
  • Pricing: The best crypto signals group features transparent pricing without any additional cost. Free crypto signals groups tend to include poor-quality signals that are less helpful. Paid groups must provide equitable pricing that corresponds to the value received. A reliable group is transparent regarding its fees and does not deceive members into paying more down the line. For low-fee trading, you can also check out our guide on the best zero-fee crypto exchanges. 
  • Learning Community: The signals group includes an engaged and helpful community. Members must be able to ask questions and share information. As you know, learning from others enhances trading ability.

Crypto Telegram signals can be a powerful tool when used correctly. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced trader, joining the right signal group can significantly impact your profitability. How We Verified These Welcome Bonus Offers?

We verified these welcome offers by checking the four criteria: offer value, trading volume requirement, expiration, and eligible regions.

  • Offer value: We separated the headline maximum from the amount a normal new user can reach. You see, a package worth 30,000 USDT may include a small sign-up reward, but a much larger futures tier for high-volume traders. We also checked whether the reward comes as withdrawable crypto, a fee rebate, a mystery box, a trading bonus, or a trial fund.
  • Trading Volume requirement: We compared the required net deposit with the spot or futures volume needed for each tier. Plus, we also checked common exclusions such as internal transfers, zero-fee trades, API activity, bot volume, and subaccounts.
  • Duration: We checked how long you have to finish a task, claim a completed reward, and use the claimed voucher. You see, every crypto exchange sign-up bonus has an expiry date, generally within 30 days of registration.
  • Eligible regions: We compared the campaign country rules with each exchange’s current restricted-location terms. A referral link may open in your browser even though your verified country cannot join the offer. We also treated U.S. versions of Binance and OKX as separate services because their global bonuses and products do not automatically carry over.

Are crypto sign-up bonuses worth it?

Yes, crypto sign-up bonuses are genuinely worth claiming in most cases, as long as you go in with realistic expectations about what you’ll actually receive. 

The instant, low-effort tiers, like Binance’s KYC voucher or even Margex’s flat $50, cost you basically nothing beyond a few minutes of setup. But again, the bigger headline numbers, like Bybit’s $30,020 or MEXC’s $10,000, require serious capital and trading volume that most casual users will never reach, so you should treat those as aspirational rather than expected.

You see, no-deposit bonus offers are rare, and a free crypto sign-up bonus with instant withdrawal usually comes with a lock, KYC step, or trading condition. The better way is to value a bonus at what you can personally use. Also, most of the bonus funds usually arrive as trading credit or vouchers rather than withdrawable cash. Hence, at least at first, read the terms before assuming you can cash out immediately.

Which crypto exchange sign-up bonus is the best for your trading type?

The best crypto sign-up bonus, or welcome reward, depends more on how you plan to use the exchange. According to the definition of crypto welcome bonus, the first-time account openers may benefit more from simple deposit or first-trade rewards, while buy-and-hold investors should look for those bonuses that never require heavy trading, and frequent traders often get more from fee discounts and similar exchange promotions.

Next, high-frequency and grid traders can usually get more value from trading-fee rebates, volume-based sign-up rewards, and futures bonuses because they trade more often.

First-Time Account Openers

First-time account openers should choose a bonus with very simple requirements and a low minimum deposit. You know, a reward for completing KYC, making your first deposit, or placing a few trades makes more sense than a large bonus that requires thousands of dollars in trading volume. Hence, you should mainly focus on how easy the reward is to unlock rather than its maximum advertised value.

Buy-and-Hold Investors

Buy-and-hold investors should look for deposit bonuses or rewards that require little trading. Basically, a $50 reward after depositing and buying crypto can be more useful than a $500 futures bonus that requires active trading. Plus, you should also avoid promotions that force you to generate high trading volume because frequent buying and selling does not match a long-term investment strategy.

High-Frequency and Grid Traders

High-frequency and grid traders can benefit most from bonuses linked to trading volume. Here, fee rebates, futures credits, trading vouchers, and volume-based rewards become more valuable because you naturally place many trades. Hence, a bonus with a higher trading requirement may therefore make sense for you, provided the normal trading fees and conditions remain competitive.

Are free crypto sign-up bonuses available for every exchange?

No, free crypto sign-up bonuses are not available on every exchange. Not every platform uses the same signup structure, and some reserve free bitcoin or similar promotions for app-based campaigns or limited regions. Basically, each platform decides its own promotion rules, and some exchanges do not offer any reward just for creating an account.

Even exchanges that advertise a welcome bonus usually ask you to complete certain steps first. So, you may need to verify your identity, deposit a minimum amount, make your first trade, or reach a required trading volume. The reward can also vary by country, campaign period, and referral link.

Can I withdraw my free crypto bonuses immediately?

No, you cannot withdraw a free crypto bonus immediately, as most exchanges place conditions on the reward because the bonus is meant to encourage real trading activity, not simply give away withdrawable cash.

You should also check the exchange app terms carefully, since bonuses can vary by region and some platforms use promotions to grow their user base.

You may need to deposit funds, complete KYC, make a certain number of trades, or reach a required trading volume before the bonus even becomes eligible for withdrawal. Plus, some rewards cannot be withdrawn at all. So, for example, futures bonuses and trading credits may only cover trading losses or fees, while you can withdraw the profits earned from them under certain rules.

Of course, this works differently from exchange to exchange. Hence, you should always check the withdrawal terms first, especially the minimum trading requirement, expiry date, and whether the bonus itself or only the profits can be withdrawn.

20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails. 

In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives.

1. Permissionless Access vs. Gatekept Accounts

For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control.

Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview:

“Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.”

With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries. 

This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms.

Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution. 

With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider.

2. 24/7 Global Settlement vs. “Banking Hours”

Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees.

Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows.

“We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.”

To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX.

This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions.

These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers.

3. Passing Yield Back to Users vs. Bank Spreads

Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed. 

In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods.

Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms.

USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital.

For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product.

4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust

Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise. 

USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification.

  • Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain.
  • Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments.
  • Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities.

Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified.

5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem

Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance.

Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems.

This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems.

The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure.

The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain

Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries.

For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work.

Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it.

PANAMA CITY, November 19, 2026 – BingX, the world’s leading multi-asset trading platform, today announced that Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) is available for trading on its platform following the company’s highly anticipated initial public offering. Eligible users can trade ANT/USDT on BingX Spot or take long and short positions through USDT-margined ANTUS(ANTHROPIC) Perpetual Futures. The launch extends BingX’s Anthropic trading offering from pre-IPO exposure to markets linked to its publicly listed stock.

Anthropic’s public listing marks a major milestone for the developer of Claude and brings one of the world’s most closely watched AI companies to public markets. The company set an initial offering price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a fully diluted valuation of up to approximately $1.4 trillion.

With ANT, BingX further expands its multi-asset offering, which includes more than 700 TradFi instruments through its perpetual futures markets, spanning stocks, indices, and commodities. ANTUS(ANTHROPIC) Perpetual Futures are available for trading 24/7, while ANT/USDT joins BingX’s U.S. stock spot offering of more than 7,000 listings, with 24/5 trading and a minimum purchase of $5. Users can access these markets alongside cryptocurrencies through a single BingX account, without needing to open a separate brokerage account.

BingX introduced Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures on May 25, giving eligible users a way to trade changes in its implied valuation before the public listing. The offering was part of BingX’s broader pre-IPO trading lineup, which has also featured companies such as SpaceX and OpenAI. 

“An IPO changes where a company trades, but our users’ interest often starts well before listing day,” said Kevin Lee, Chief Strategy Officer of BingX. “With Anthropic, users could trade changes in its implied valuation ahead of the IPO. Now they can trade alongside stocks, commodities, currencies and crypto through the same BingX account. Connecting opportunities across markets and across different stages of a company’s journey is an important part of how we’re building the BingX multi-asset ecosystem.”

To mark the launch, BingX is introducing the Anthropic IPO Trading Contest, offering eligible participants the opportunity to compete for a total of up to 150,000 USDT in individual rewards. Rankings will be determined by eligible contract trading volume, giving participants an additional opportunity to engage with the newly listed asset.

About BingX 

Founded in 2018, BingX is the world’s leading multi-asset trading platform, serving more than 40 million users worldwide. From crypto to traditional markets, BingX connects users with a broad range of assets and opportunities across global markets through one unified platform.

With perpetual futures, TradFi offerings, spot trading and copy trading, alongside AI-powered innovations, BingX delivers a reliable, intelligent, and responsive trading experience designed to help traders navigate evolving markets and act on opportunities with greater confidence and efficiency.

BingX has been the Principal Partner of Chelsea FC since 2024 and became the Official Team Partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP in 2026.
